🔧 CLOSURE-DISCIPLINE POSTURE (load-bearing, pre-completion anchor)

When closing a fix/audit/cleanup task, "resolved" requires THREE assertions:

  1. UPSTREAM CONTROL — file path of the resolver in the pipeline,
     not "I ran the script." If the fix is a one-shot script that
     could need re-running for new entities, it is downstream-only.

  2. CATCH-NET — chain_audit invariant ID, test, or explicit
     "no catch-net possible because…" justification. The audit
     should flag this gap if it regresses.

  3. PIPELINE SURVIVAL — will this fix survive the next render_all
     or equivalent pipeline run? If a downstream stage can wipe it
     (the compute-cvrs regex sibling-wipe pattern), the fix isn't
     stable and "resolved" is wrong.

If ALL three hold: status: resolved with upstream_control_path: and
catch_mechanism: fields populated.

If ANY are missing: status: symptom-repaired, upstream-pending —
with a follow-up signal capturing what the upstream control would
need to be.

FORBIDDEN closure-claim patterns (will be blocked by Layer 4 Stop hook):

  • Ending response with "complete / done / resolved / fixed / shipped"
    without any mention of upstream control, pipeline integration,
    catch-net invariant, or future-regression prevention
  • Writing a signal file with status: resolved without
    upstream_control_path: and catch_mechanism: fields
  • Declaring a wave/audit/sweep "closed" while the pattern that
    produced the gap is still live
  • Declaring victory based on running a one-shot patch script

Reinforcement history: Brien has reinforced the closure-DoD policy
multiple times. Memory entries (feedback_errors_are_signals,
feedback_audit_vs_writethrough, reference_signal_closure_policy) and
the existing signal-stream.md DoD library haven't closed the drift.
This hook IS the mechanism-level fix.

<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

Run a session-start overwatch sweep. Execute ALL checks in parallel where possible. Report findings as a single status board at the end.

## 0. Location Mode & Peripheral Presence

Before any other check, run `Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/peripheral-presence.sh` to determine which physical peripherals are currently attached. Parse the JSON. Cache the result for the rest of the sweep.

**Modes:**
- `studio` — full studio rig attached; probe all peripheral connectors.
- `mobile` — laptop-only (on the road); skip peripheral connectors, mark as `⏭ EXPECTED-ABSENT — mobile mode`.
- `auto` (default) — use USB/Thunderbolt enumeration to decide per-peripheral.

**Peripheral-dependent checks** (treat as ⏭ EXPECTED-ABSENT when absent, ✅/⚠️ when present):
- Elgato Stream Deck (`streamdeck` field)
- Microphones / audio interfaces (`elgato_audio` field)
- External display–dependent diagnostics (`external_display` field)

**Critical:** the MCP-process-health check (Section 7) MUST still run for these connectors regardless of presence. A peripheral being unplugged is expected; orphaned plugin processes when the device is absent is *more* suspicious, not less. Report as "orphaned plugin processes (device not attached)" rather than the standard "duplicate PIDs" warning when peripheral is absent but processes are running.

Also check the current session model (available from system context or `claude --version`). If the session model is `claude-sonnet-4-6` or any non-Opus model: emit a ⚠️ warning in the status board and add to Issues Found: "Session running on [model] — autonomy grant compliance is degraded on Sonnet; L4 decisions may require extra reinforcement. Recommend restarting on Opus 4.7 for execution work." (See SIG-2026-05-07-autonomy-grant-drift-sonnet-sessions.)

Report mode + presence as the first two rows of the status board:
```
| Location mode | ✅/ℹ️ | mode=auto, streamdeck=false, elgato_audio=false, external_display=true |
| Session model | ✅/⚠️ | claude-opus-4-7 (execution-safe) OR claude-sonnet-4-6 ⚠️ autonomy grants degraded |
```

## 1. Anthropic Status Check
Fetch https://status.claude.com/ and report any active incidents, degraded services, or outages. If all clear, report uptime percentages for Claude API and Claude Code.

## 2. CLAUDE.md Integrity
Compare ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (global) and ~/CLAUDE.md (project-level) for drift. Report whether they are identical or list specific differences. Then spot-check that all folder paths referenced in CLAUDE.md actually exist on disk:
- Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/Subaru/
- Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/ASA/
- Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/Turnberry/
- Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/FidelityGuaranty/
- Workspaces/Core/products/forge/

## 3. Memory Index Consistency (Write-Through Validation — SIG-028)
Read ~/.claude/projects/-Users-brien-Workspaces/memory/MEMORY.md. For each entry:
- Verify the linked file exists
- Compare the one-line summary against the file's actual content (check key numbers, statuses, counts)

**When staleness is found, apply write-through triage:**

Products WITH write-through hooks (do NOT fix inline — signal instead):
- `project_skills_architecture.md` / `project_executable_ip_taxonomy.md` → hook: `register-skill.sh --sync`
- `project_unified_persona_system.md` → hook: persona-intake Stage 6 / `register-skill.sh --sync`
- glossary.md engagement table → hook: `engagement-onboarding.sh`

For these files: if stale, emit "**WRITE-THROUGH FAILURE:** [file] is stale — hook `[hook name]` did not fire or failed" in the Issues Found section. Do NOT fix inline.

Products WITHOUT write-through hooks yet (grace period — fix inline):
- All other memory files (brand, migration, MCP config, studio control, etc.)

For these: fix inline as before, but note "(no write-through hook — fixing inline, grace period)" in the report.

**Consecutive clean sweeps counter:** Track how many consecutive overwatch runs found 0 stale memory entries. Report the count. Goal: 3+ consecutive clean sweeps validates that write-through hooks are working.

## 4. Glossary Federation Health (SIG-028 — write-through validated)
Verify Workspaces/memory/glossary.md exists (canonical). Verify all engagement glossaries listed in the "Active engagement glossaries" table actually exist on disk.

**Write-through hook:** `engagement-onboarding.sh` (at Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/) scans engagement folders and syncs the glossary table. If an engagement folder has a glossary.md but is missing from the central table, this is a write-through failure — report it as such, do NOT fix inline.

Also verify: each engagement glossary still references `memory/glossary.md` as its central hub.

## 5. MCP Connector Probes
Ping each registered connector with a lightweight call to verify auth is live. Run all probes in parallel.

**Google Workspace precedence (load-bearing):** For Gmail / Calendar / Drive, ALWAYS probe the Anthropic native connectors FIRST. `workspace-mcp` (`mcp__google-workspace__*`) is a **FALLBACK** — never the primary probe. See `memory/feedback_prefer_native_anthropic_connectors.md` for full rule. A workspace-mcp `auth-required` error reported as a Gmail/Calendar/Drive failure is a category error — reach for the native tool, do not surface the OAuth URL.

**Known connectors (probe with these calls):**

| Service | Native tool (probe FIRST) | Fallback (probe ONLY if native fails) |
|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Gmail | `mcp__2af7d4b6-48e4-40e0-b692-83bb17863698__list_labels` (pageSize=1) | `mcp__google-workspace__search_gmail_messages` |
| Google Calendar | `mcp__e84bacfb-2d7e-4832-93d8-cd99572ef756__list_calendars` (pageSize=1) | `mcp__google-workspace__list_calendars` |
| Google Drive | `REDACTED` (pageSize=1) | `mcp__google-workspace__search_drive_files` |

Report Gmail/Calendar/Drive as **a single row each** with status reflecting the native probe. If native LIVE and workspace-mcp FAILED, that is NOT a failure — note "(fallback workspace-mcp auth pending; native primary live)" in the detail column, do NOT flag as a critical issue.

Other connectors (no precedence concern):
- GitHub: search for theparlor/skills-engine
- Slack: search for #general (limit 1)
- Jira/Confluence: getAccessibleAtlassianResources
- Harvest: get_current_user
- Miro: board_list_items or context_get (any lightweight call — ASA boards are active)
- Granola: list_meetings (limit 1) or get_meetings (Brien uses for meeting transcripts)
- Elgato Stream Deck: get_executable_actions (studio-control plugin) — **gated on Section 0 `streamdeck=true`**; otherwise mark `⏭ EXPECTED-ABSENT — peripheral not attached`
- Library Index: library_stats (custom MCP at Core/products/library-index-mcp/)
- Office suite (Excel/Word/PowerPoint): get_document_text (AppleScript-based, no cloud auth — tests local Office install)
- Scheduled Tasks: list_scheduled_tasks

**Cold-start re-probe rule:** Cloud connectors (Harvest, native Google connectors) may timeout on first probe after a cold start. If a cloud connector fails, wait 5 seconds and re-probe ONCE before marking FAILED. Only report FAILED after two consecutive failures.

**New connector detection:** Before probing, scan the available MCP tool list for any connector prefixes not in the known list above. If new connectors are found:
1. Probe them with the most lightweight identity/list call available
2. Report them in the status board as NEW + LIVE/FAILED
3. Recommend adding them to this checklist permanently

Report each connector as LIVE or FAILED with the specific error.

## 7. MCP Process Health
Check for duplicate MCP server processes (known issue — anthropics/claude-code#42866). Run: `ps aux | grep mcp | grep -v grep` and flag any server with more than one PID. **Expected: 2 PIDs per server** (one for Chat/Cowork, one for Code). Only flag servers with **3+ PIDs** as duplicates. If duplicates found, report which server and recommend killing the stale process. Google Workspace OAuth will break silently if workspace-mcp is duplicated.

## 8. Usage Tracking & Burn Rate Forecast

Parse Claude Code session logs to measure token consumption since the weekly reset (Friday 11:00 AM ET).

**Data sources:** `~/.claude/projects/-Users-brien-Workspaces/*.jsonl` — filter by modification time since last Friday 11am.

**Collect per-session:**
- Model turns (count of `"model":"claude-opus-4-6"` vs `"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6"` vs `"model":"claude-haiku-4-5"`)
- Output tokens (sum of `"output_tokens"`)
- Cache creation tokens (sum of `"cache_creation_input_tokens"`)
- Cache read tokens (sum of `"cache_read_input_tokens"`)

**Also scan subagent logs:** `~/.claude/projects/-Users-brien-Workspaces/*/subagents/*.jsonl`

**Compute:**
- Hours elapsed since weekly reset
- % of week elapsed (168 hours total)
- Burn ratio: budget% / time% (under 1.0 = sustainable, over 1.0 = will exceed)
- Projected weekly total (linear extrapolation)
- Opus vs Sonnet turn ratio

**Report format:**
```
### Usage & Forecast
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Week elapsed | X% (Xh of 168h) |
| All Models consumed | X% (from dashboard or estimated) |
| Opus turns | X |
| Sonnet turns | X |
| Output tokens | XM |
| Burn ratio | X.Xx |
| Projected weekly | X% |
| Sonnet bucket | X% |

Forecast: [SUSTAINABLE / WATCH / THROTTLE] — [explanation]
```

**Thresholds (report the flag, no commentary):**
- SUSTAINABLE: projected <70%
- WATCH: projected 70-90%
- THROTTLE: projected >90%

**Estimated API cost of current consumption (corrected 2026-07-08, RETRO-2026-04-09-overwatch-SIG-4 + SIG-2026-07-08-overwatch-section8-cost-formula-crossrepo-followup):** the prior version summed raw jsonl `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` across the whole session and priced the total at flat Opus retail rates. That is a category error, not a multiplier error: those fields are gross per-turn token movement (a long session resends its growing context on every turn), and Brien is on the Max plan's weekly quota, not pay-per-token billing. Retail $/MTok pricing only applies to genuine Extra Usage overflow. Combining gross resent-context volume with retail-only pricing produced a roughly 100x overstatement in the 2026-04-09 incident (jsonl estimate $5,011.14 vs. dashboard-reported $54.06 Extra Usage spent).

**Primary approach (no computed dollar figure for in-quota consumption):**
1. Report Opus/Sonnet/Haiku turn counts (accurate as counts) and the dashboard-reported "% consumed" (from a Settings > Usage screenshot, or "from dashboard or estimated" per the existing report line).
2. If Extra Usage is enabled and overflow occurred, read the dollar figure directly from the dashboard's own "Extra usage: $X spent" line. Do not compute it.
3. If no dashboard capture is available this session, state "No dashboard capture this session, dollar figure not computed" rather than falling back silently to a token-sum estimate.

**Fallback (labeled gross-movement ceiling estimate only, never presented as billed cost):** if a directional estimate is still wanted absent a dashboard capture, compute it per model class generically, not by flattening everything to one model's rate. Apply each class's own input/output rate, deriving cache pricing as a multiple of that class's input rate: `cache write = 1.25 x input`, `cache read = 0.1 x input`.

| Model class | Input/MTok | Output/MTok | Cache write/MTok (1.25x input) | Cache read/MTok (0.1x input) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opus-class (e.g. Opus 4.8) | $5 | $25 | $6.25 | $0.50 |
| Sonnet-class (e.g. Sonnet 5) | $2 | $10 | $2.50 | $0.20 |

Sum `(output_tokens x output_rate) + (cache_creation_tokens x cache_write_rate) + (cache_read_tokens x cache_read_rate) + (input_tokens x input_rate)` per model class, then add the per-class totals. Do not apply Opus rates to Sonnet/Haiku turns or vice versa. Label the result explicitly: "gross token-movement ceiling estimate, NOT billed cost, see dashboard for actual spend." Reference: `Core/reference/usage-tracker/usage-model.md` for the full pricing table and overflow economics.

**This section is telemetry only.** No strategy recommendations, no model selection advice, no philosophy. If Brien wants to discuss usage strategy, that's a separate session.

## 10. Session Signal: Engagement File Activity

## 11. Incestuous Amplification Detection

> Grounded in: Boyd's OODA loop theory, Richards (Chet Richards, *Necesse*, 2020), RAT-003. Boyd identified that the IG&C feedback from Orient back to Observe creates the most dangerous organizational pathology: the knowledge base filters observations to confirm itself, creating a self-reinforcing loop disconnected from reality. Richards calls this "incestuous amplification." Boyd's prescription: "you need outside reference points." Overwatch is that external reference point — but only if it explicitly looks for what the system is NOT seeing.

Run these three checks on the knowledge base, persona system, and signal log. This is NOT lint — lint catches structural gaps. This catches confirmation bias.

### 11a. Disconfirmation Check

For each active persona (from `Core/products/cast/farm/registry/`), active DDR (from `Workspaces/.context/DECISIONS.md`), and active theme (from active engagement knowledge bases):

1. State the core claim or position the artifact makes
2. Explicitly ask: **what evidence would contradict or limit this claim?**
3. Search the knowledge base, signal log, and recent session journals for any such contradicting evidence
4. Report: "confirmed — no contradicting evidence found" OR "tension detected — [artifact] vs. [contradicting signal/finding]"

This is not "is it stale?" — it's "is it wrong, or overconfident?" A persona can be perfectly fresh and still be wrong.

### 11b. Signal Diversity Audit

> **Coverage fix (2026-05-06, SIG-2026-05-06-overwatch-engagement-signal-discovery-gap):** The prior procedure examined only workspace-level signal dirs and missed engagement-local and product-local silos entirely. Subaru was falsely flagged as a dark zone when it had 7 in-window signals in its own `.intent/signals/`. The procedure below replaces that with a full enumeration sweep.

**Step 1 — Build the enumeration list at runtime.**

Dynamically discover all `.intent/signals/` locations by scanning these root directories:
- `Core/products/*/` — one entry per product subdirectory
- `Work/Consulting/Engagements/*/` — one entry per engagement
- `Work/Advising/Engagements/*/` — one entry per advising engagement
- `Core/frameworks/*/` — one entry per framework (e.g., intent, coherence-engineering)
- Workspace-level: `Workspaces/.intent/signals/` (existing)
- Optional/personal: `Home/TheParlor/Renovation/` if `.intent/` exists there

Do NOT hardcode paths. Use `find` or equivalent directory listing against each root at sweep time so newly created engagements and products are discovered automatically.

**Step 2 — For each enumerated path, classify into exactly three states:**

- `no_intent_dir` — neither `.intent/` nor `.intent/signals/` exists at this path. This is a **structural gap** — worse than dormancy. It means signal discipline has not been established here at all.
- `intent_empty_in_window` — `.intent/signals/` exists but contains zero files with mtime in the last 14 days (computed dynamically from current date, not hardcoded). This is **true dormancy** or a signal-discipline gap.
- `intent_active_in_window` — `.intent/signals/` exists and has one or more files with mtime in the last 14 days. This path is **NOT a dark zone**.

**Step 3 — Compute the 14-day window dynamically.**

The window is `[today - 14 days, today]`. Do not hardcode date strings. Use `find -mtime -14` or equivalent. This ensures the window stays current on every run.

**Step 4 — Filter bulk-touch noise.**

When computing "files modified in window," exclude file groups where N≥5 files share identical second-precision mtime across distinct directories. This is mtime pollution from filesystem sweep operations, not genuine signal activity. Reference: `SIG-2026-05-06-bulk-touch-sweep-mtime-pollution` for the specific pattern. When bulk-touch noise is excluded, note "(N files excluded — bulk-touch mtime pollution)" in the finding.

**Step 5 — Domain cluster counts.**

After classifying all paths, count signals by domain cluster across all `intent_active_in_window` paths combined:
- Cluster assignments: governance, research, skills, personas, engagements, infrastructure, personal
- Identify which clusters have zero in-window signals (across ALL paths, not just workspace-level)
- Distinguish: cluster absent because no work in that area (acceptable) vs. cluster absent despite active work there (signal-discipline gap)

**Step 6 — Dark zone determination.**

A path is a **DARK ZONE** only if ALL of the following are true:
- It is `intent_empty_in_window` (not `no_intent_dir` — that's a structural gap, a separate finding)
- AND it is an active project area (listed in CLAUDE.md project sections OR modified in the last 30 days by non-signal files, **excluding bulk-touch mtime groups** — apply the same N≥5 identical-second-precision filter from Step 4 to the 30-day activity check)

A path in `no_intent_dir` state is reported as **STRUCTURAL GAP**, not dark zone.
A path in `intent_active_in_window` state is explicitly reported as **ACTIVE — not a dark zone**.

**Report format for 11b:**

```
#### Signal Coverage — Enumerated Paths

| Path | State | In-window count | Classification |
|------|-------|-----------------|----------------|
| Work/Consulting/Engagements/Subaru | intent_active_in_window | 7 | ACTIVE |
| Work/Consulting/Engagements/Turnberry | intent_active_in_window | 1 | ACTIVE |
| Core/products/loom | intent_empty_in_window | 0 | DARK ZONE (active product) |
| Core/products/topography | intent_empty_in_window | 0 | DARK ZONE (active product) |
```

### 11c. Source Freshness vs. Conclusion Freshness

A conclusion can be stale even when its source documents are current. This happens when the field has reinterpreted the underlying sources but our compiled interpretation hasn't updated.

> **Field reference fix (2026-05-07, SIG-2026-05-07-freshening-schedule-last-freshened-backfill):** The prior procedure read a `freshened_at` field that does not exist in either the registry YAMLs or the schedule. The actual field name in both sources is `last_freshened`. Procedure below uses the correct field and adds age-aware HIGH_RISK thresholds.

**Authoritative source:** `Core/products/cast/farm/freshening-schedule.yaml` is canonical for staleness tracking — it colocates `cadence`, `last_freshened`, `last_freshened_approximated`, and `next_check` per entity. Registry YAMLs (`Core/products/cast/farm/registry/[slug].yaml`) carry a mirror `last_freshened` field but are not authoritative for schedule decisions.

> **Field semantics (PS-016, 2026-05-27):** `next_check` is the single authoritative scheduled-run date. `cadence` is the rule used to compute the NEXT `next_check` after a freshening run: `new_next_check = freshened_date + cadence_offset_days`. For never-freshened entries, `next_check` is set at entry-creation time and is already correct — do NOT fall back to `registry.created` when `last_freshened` is null.

**Procedure — for each entry in `freshening-schedule.yaml`:**

1. Read `next_check` directly:
   - If `next_check` is present: compute `days_overdue = today - next_check` (negative = not yet due)
   - If `next_check` is absent: DATA_GAP — file a signal, do not flag HIGH_RISK or attempt to infer from cadence

2. Apply status rule:
   - `days_overdue < 0` (today before next_check) → **OK** — not yet due
   - `0 <= days_overdue <= 15` → **MONITOR** — due, within grace window
   - `days_overdue > 15` → **HIGH_RISK** — overdue beyond grace window
   - `next_check` absent → **DATA_GAP** — note and skip

   > **Critical:** null `last_freshened` alone is NOT a HIGH_RISK signal. A persona may be never-freshened and still have a valid future `next_check`. Do not apply cadence math to `last_freshened` or `registry.created` to compute overdue status.

3. **`last_freshened_approximated: true` handling:** Informational context only. Apply the `next_check`-based rule above; do not adjust thresholds for approximated dates.

4. Lightweight semantic check (only for HIGH_RISK candidates): since `last_freshened`, has the field produced significant new work by or about this person that would change the synthesis? This is heuristic — a full harvest happens via `persona-intake` re-run, not in overwatch.

**Output format:** report each HIGH_RISK persona as a row with: `slug | cadence | next_check | days_overdue | last_freshened | recommended_action` (where action is typically "re-run persona-intake" or "schedule manual freshening").

Report any persona where conclusion staleness risk is HIGH. If all entries are within thresholds, report: "All freshening entries within cadence thresholds."

### 11c-exec. Freshening Executor Liveness (the executor itself, not per-persona)

11c checks whether each persona's CONCLUSION is stale. This checks whether the nightly freshening EXECUTOR (`com.brien.cast-freshening-nightly` calling `claude -p`) actually RAN. A transient failure (e.g. 2026-06-24 "API socket closed", zero output, no digest) leaves nothing for 11c to catch. Codified as `chain_audit.py` invariant `INV-FRESHEN-EXECUTOR-LIVENESS`; this Section is the session-start runner because `chain_audit` is not scheduled and its report goes stale.

**Procedure:**

1. Newest output: glob `Core/products/cast/farm/corpus/*/freshening-*.md` and take the newest `YYYY-MM-DD` from the filenames. `age = today - that date`. `age >= 2 days` is a **WARN** (a full nightly missed); `age >= 5 days` is a hard concern.
2. Today's run errored: if `Core/products/cast/engine/logs/launchd-freshening-<today>.log` exists and contains `"is_error":true` but NOT `Freshen complete`, the run fired but produced no digest. **WARN**.
3. If either fires, surface newest-output date, age, and (if errored) the log name, with recommended action: inspect the log and re-run the freshening executor. Apply the same signal-aware correlation as elsewhere (a `resolved` SIG dated after the failure clears it).

If neither fires, report: "Freshening executor live (newest output YYYY-MM-DD)."

## 12. Intent-Site Evolves-Not-Deprecates Drift (governance catch-net)

Guards the intent-site "deprecating" anti-pattern. **Canon (SIG-INTENTSITE-2026-04-23, affirmed by DEC-004):** intent-site EVOLVES IN PLACE into the Intent + Throughline / system-plane surface — it does NOT deprecate at launch. Full deprecation of the standalone identity is gated on Phase 3 (eventual Stage 4). Any *descriptive* Core doc that couples "intent-site" with a bald "deprecat" claim lacking an evolves/gated qualifier is drift against canon.

**Executable check (main thread — grep-based, sub-second):**

`Core/frameworks/intent-site/scripts/check-evolves-not-deprecates.sh [scan_root]`

- Default scan root: `~/Workspaces/Core` (traverses the gitignored sibling product repos parallax/warp, which are physically on disk).
- **Exit 0** — clean. Prints the count of intent-site refs scanned.
- **Exit 1** — DRIFT: one or more descriptive docs couple intent-site with an unqualified "deprecat" claim. The script prints each offending `file:line`.
- **Exit 2** — the scan could not run (broken tool/path or failed sanity gate). **Fails CLOSED** — treat as a finding, never a pass.

Historical records under `.intent/` and frozen `archive/` eras are excluded by the script on purpose — they legitimately quote the old stance as point-in-time fact.

**Surface in the status board:**

```
| Governance: intent-site evolves | ✅/⚠️/❌ | exit 0 = clean (N refs) · exit 1 = DRIFT · exit 2 = scan failed (fail-closed) |
```

Status map: exit 0 → ✅; exit 1 → ⚠️ and list each offending `file:line` in Issues Found under the label **[ISD]** (Intent-Site Deprecation drift); exit 2 → ❌ and surface the script's stderr in Issues Found — the scan is broken, so do not trust any "clean" reading until it is fixed.

**Classification — surface only (catch-net, not write-through).** Do NOT auto-edit offending docs. Resolving a flagged line is a judgment call: either add an evolves/gated qualifier to the descriptive line, or — if the line is a legitimate point-in-time record — move it under `.intent/`. The script is the recurrence-prevention catch-net for SIG-EXEC-2026-06-05-ecosystem-deprecation-correction; this section is its auto-invocation.

**Signal-aware:** if a signal with `status: resolved` already covers a specific instance the script flags, elide it per the standard signal-aware correlation table (same handling as Sections 9 and 11).

## 13. Product-Repo Working-Tree Residue Aging (governance catch-net)

Guards the recompute-without-commit anti-pattern: an autonomous or session run of `--apply` tooling mutates hundreds of tracked files in a nested product repo and ends without committing, so large residue sits in the working tree with nothing flagging its age. **Worked example (SIG-RESIDUE-DISPOSITION-recompute-2026-07-01-committed-2026-07-02, cast):** a 2026-07-01 recompute session left 949 dirty entries across 900+ tracked files in `Core/products/cast`; the residue sat for 2 days, blocked clean git pulls, and forced every agent into staging workarounds before it was characterized and committed.

**Executable check (main thread — sub-second per repo):**

`Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/check-product-repo-residue.sh [root] [count_threshold] [age_hours]`

- Default scan roots (widened 2026-07-08, after `Core/frameworks/coherence-engineering` sat with 16 dirty files for three weeks unseen): `~/Workspaces/Core/products` AND `~/Workspaces/Core/frameworks`, every immediate child of either root that is its own git repo (nested product/framework repos per `reference_product_repos_nested`). Passing an explicit root positionally scans ONLY that one root, preserving the original single-root contract exactly (same output wording, same exit codes).
- **Flags a repo when EITHER** dirty entries (`git status --porcelain`) exceed 50, **OR** any dirty TRACKED file's mtime is older than 24h.
- **Exit 0** — clean. Prints the count of product repos scanned.
- **Exit 1** — RESIDUE: prints per flagged repo the dirty-entry count, aged-tracked count + oldest age, dominant path pattern, and suggested disposition.
- **Exit 2** — the scan could not run (bad root, git missing, no repos found). **Fails CLOSED** — treat as a finding, never a pass.

**Surface in the status board:**

```
| Governance: product-repo residue | ✅/⚠️/❌ | exit 0 = clean (N repos) · exit 1 = RESIDUE (N repos flagged) · exit 2 = scan failed (fail-closed) |
```

Status map: exit 0 → ✅; exit 1 → ⚠️ and list each flagged repo in Issues Found under the label **[RES]** (Residue) with count, oldest age, and dominant path pattern; exit 2 → ❌ and surface the script's stderr in Issues Found.

**Classification — surface only (catch-net, not write-through).** Do NOT auto-commit or auto-discard. The disposition protocol per the worked example: (1) characterize the residue — which run produced it (`repo-hygiene-sweep.py` classifies by source class A/B/C/D), is it byte-identical to what the tooling computes today (idempotency dry-run)?; (2) then commit-or-discard as ONE deliberate act, with a disposition signal. A single aged file is often class-D in-flight human work — judgment, not auto-flag-to-fix; the bulk-residue pattern (high count, uniform path prefix, tool-generated) is the real target. The durable upstream control remains producer-side write-through (`commit-outputs.sh` registration for the producing run) — when the same repo recurs across sweeps, that recurrence IS the signal to install it.

**Signal-aware:** if a disposition signal with `status: resolved` (or an `active` in-flight-work signal) already covers a flagged repo's residue, elide or annotate per the standard signal-aware correlation table (same handling as Sections 9, 11, and 12).

## 15. Local Toolchain Currency (read-only reporter)

Guards the silent-toolchain-drift anti-pattern: local developer tools (Homebrew formulae, npm globals, pip, the codeburn CLI) fall out of date with nothing surfacing the drift at session start, so a manual audit is the only way it ever gets noticed. **Worked example (2026-07-06):** an ad-hoc audit found node, ollama, git, and ~40 brew formulae plus several npm globals silently outdated. Brien's directive: fold a READ-ONLY currency check into a recurring surface, a reporter that lets him approve upgrades, never one that auto-upgrades. Unattended major bumps (node 25 to 26, ollama 0.18 to 0.31) are the exact failure mode this must not trigger.

**Executable check (main thread; read-only):**

`Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/check-toolchain-currency.sh`

- Reports counts + names of outdated Homebrew formulae/pinned casks, npm globals, and pip packages, plus codeburn by name. Does NOT run `brew update`, `brew upgrade`, `npm install`, or `pip install`: zero writes to any package manager.
- Bounded per-probe by TOOLCHAIN_PROBE_TIMEOUT (default 20s) when coreutils `timeout`/`gtimeout` is present; runs unbounded otherwise (pip is the slow probe, it queries PyPI).
- Exit 0 = all probeable toolchains current (or none installed). Exit 1 = updates available (INFORMATIONAL: prints counts + names). Exit 2 = every present package-manager probe failed, FAILS CLOSED (treat as a finding, never a pass).

**Surface in the status board:**

```
| Local: toolchain currency | ✅/ℹ️/❌ | exit 0 = current · exit 1 = N updates available (informational) · exit 2 = scan failed (fail-closed) |
```

Status map: exit 0 = ✅; exit 1 = ℹ️ and list the SUMMARY line (brew/npm/pip/codeburn counts) in Issues Found under the label **[TCC]** (ToolChain Currency); exit 2 = ❌ and surface the script's stderr. Exit 1 is INFORMATIONAL, not a governance failure: "updates available" is the normal steady state, and holding a major bump is a valid Brien decision.

**Classification: surface only, NEVER auto-upgrade.** This is the read-only half by design. It exists as a reporter and not an upgrader precisely because unattended `brew upgrade` / `npm update -g` is the failure mode being guarded against (a blind major bump breaks a working toolchain). Disposition (upgrade now, hold, or upgrade a safe subset) is a Brien call every time. There is intentionally no write-through resolver here: an auto-upgrade catch-net would defeat the safety property, so recurrence (new versions shipping) is expected and acceptable, drained by re-running this reporter on demand.

**Signal-aware:** if a signal with `status: resolved` records that a specific package was deliberately held (e.g. node/ollama pinned for a reason), annotate rather than re-surface it per the standard signal-aware correlation table (same handling as Sections 9, 11, 12, 13).

## 16. Repo History Divergence (governance catch-net)

Guards the silent local/remote fork anti-pattern: a nested product or framework repo (or the Workspaces root) drifts from its remote when a bot or cloud session advances one line while local sessions keep committing on the other, and nothing looks until the two histories are far apart. **Worked example (2026-07-02, `Core/frameworks/intent`):** a remote PR burst landed hours after the local clone's last pull; the clone even fetched on 07-03 so `git status -sb` showed ahead/behind from day one, but no sweep looked, and 17 days later the stack was 26 local-only vs 24 remote-only commits, two lines had minted colliding DDR-009 ids, and a triage pass had audited a stale world. The sibling residue lens (Section 13) asks "is the working tree dirty?"; this asks "are two committed histories growing apart?".

**Executable check (main thread; read-only, fetches per repo):**

`Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/check-repo-divergence.sh [--root DIR]... [--repo DIR]... [--behind-max N] [--ahead-age-hours H] [--no-fetch]`

- Default scan: every immediate child of `~/Workspaces/Core/products` and `~/Workspaces/Core/frameworks` that is its own git repo, plus the Workspaces root repo. Fetch-before-compute is the DEFAULT (a stale tracking ref under-counts `behind` — exactly how the seed incident hid for 16 days); a per-repo fetch failure degrades that repo to its last-fetched ref, stamps `fetch_failed: true`, and never aborts the sweep. Pass `--no-fetch` for offline runs.
- **Flags a repo when EITHER** ahead > 0 AND the last local commit is older than 24h (committed work sitting unpushed past a working day), **OR** behind > 20 (the remote has run far ahead unintegrated). Fresh ahead-work (< 24h) is in-flight session work and is never flagged; a repo with no upstream is reported NO-UPSTREAM but not flagged.
- Emits one signal per flagged repo per day (idempotent, never rewritten): `.intent/signals/SIG-REPO-DIVERGENCE-<repo>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`.
- **Exit 0** — clean (prints repos scanned). **Exit 1** — DIVERGENCE (prints per flagged repo: ahead/behind counts vs upstream, last-local-commit age, reason). **Exit 2** — scan could not run (bad root, git missing, zero repos). **Fails CLOSED** — treat as a finding, never a pass.

**Surface in the status board:**

```
| Governance: repo divergence | ✅/⚠️/❌ | exit 0 = clean (N repos) · exit 1 = DIVERGENCE (N flagged) · exit 2 = scan failed (fail-closed) |
```

Status map: exit 0 → ✅; exit 1 → ⚠️ and list each flagged repo in Issues Found under the label **[DIV]** (Divergence) with ahead/behind counts and last-commit age; exit 2 → ❌ and surface the script's stderr.

**Classification — surface only, and reconcile, never park (catch-net, not write-through).** Do NOT auto-merge, auto-push, or rebase a long shared-history divergence. Disposition per the seed's worked example: fetch, read BOTH sides (each line may have minted ids or audited state the other cannot see — this is analysis work, not a mechanical "N conflicts, yours to sort"), merge with a single merge commit, run the repo's test surface, push. Do NOT park it: every additional local commit deepens the eventual reconciliation, and parking-instead-of-reconciling was itself flagged (`.intent/signals/SIG-2026-07-19-divergence-parked-instead-of-reconciled.md`; memory `feedback_merge_conflicts_are_analysis_work`). Worked example: `Core/frameworks/intent/.intent/signals/SIG-2026-07-19-intent-repo-divergence-reconciled.md`.

**Signal-aware:** if a `SIG-REPO-DIVERGENCE-*` signal with `status: resolved` (a landed reconciliation) already covers a flagged repo, elide or annotate per the standard signal-aware correlation table (same handling as Sections 9, 11, 12, 13, 15).

# A handoff asserted a before-state its own repo already contradicted, and the plan it carried could not run

## What the handoff asserted
"The status was drained on 2026-07-23. Nothing else was done in production. The status
still exists there." On that basis it carried a two-step plan: remove the status from
`MARS AgileTest Workflow`, then delete it.

## What production showed
The second sentence was true. The first was not. The workflow removal had already been
done, by hand in the Jira admin UI, on 2026-07-23 at 17:39 UTC. Three independent reads
agree: the workflow went from versionNumber 1 (statuses include 15571) to versionNumber 3
(they do not); the new-API read of the workflow does not contain the string 15571
anywhere; and the audit log holds two `Workflow updated` records 1.3 seconds apart with
the two-phase temp-copy signature.

Consequence: the plan could not run at all. Step 1 halted at validation with
`OLD_STATUS_MISSING_IN_ORIGINAL_WORKFLOW`, and because the applier stops rather than skip,
step 2 was never reached. A delete-only plan had to be written before anything could
execute.

## The part that makes this a signal rather than a mistake

=== HIT 2: glyph violation ===
---
title: 78 of 79 Forge skill files violate the no-glyph house rule; the render pipeline has no glyph gate
type: signal
status: open
severity: medium
created: 2026-07-20
origin_session: 38e18269-e2c2-4c47-85ba-b9eaa809663d
discovered_by: narrate-skill build agent (incidental), verified by parent 2026-07-20
---

WHAT THIS IS, PLAINLY. Brien has a hard rule: no em-dashes, en-dashes, arrow glyphs, or ellipsis characters in anything shareable, because his peers read those as an AI tell and it blocks him from sharing the work. His Claude Code skill library is shareable intellectual property. Measured 2026-07-20 by grep across /Users/brien/Workspaces/Core/products/forge/outputs/claude-code: 78 of the 79 skill files contain at least one of those forbidden glyphs. Only the skill created today (narrate) is clean. So the library that is meant to be shareable currently fails Brien's own sharing bar, top to bottom.

WHY IT MATTERS. The rule is now enforced going forward by a Stop hook, but the hook only catches chat responses, not the on-disk skill files, and the library predates the enforcement. Every one of these 78 files is a document Brien cannot hand to a peer without it reading as machine-authored.

So even after a cleanup, the next render can reintroduce glyphs and no one is told. # Brien's Workspaces - Claude Entry Point

> **Read order**: (1) `Core/frameworks/protocols/FIRST_BRAIN_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md` - how to think, when to act, why. (2) This file - facts, structure, entry points. (3) Domain-specific CLAUDE.md for wherever you're working.

## Operating System (Read First)

`Core/frameworks/protocols/FIRST_BRAIN_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md` - Brien's decision heuristics, strategic context, pattern library, autonomy framework, and working partnership norms. This is the agency layer that governs judgment and initiative. Read it before doing anything substantive.

## Governance Chain (Rule 25 - always walk the full chain before organizing)

1. `Workspaces/AGENTS.md` - **authoritative placement resolver** (wins all conflicts)
2. `Workspaces/.context/DECISIONS.md` - **design rationale** (WS-DDR records - why the system looks this way)
3. `Core/products/digital-declutter/RULES.md` - behavioral rules for declutter operations
4. `Core/products/digital-declutter/references/workspaces-structure.md` - v4.0 structure spec
5. `Core/products/digital-declutter/references/context-md-template.md` - CONTEXT.md template
6. `Core/products/digital-declutter/references/engagement-index-template.md` - v4.0 engagement schema
7. `Core/templates/schemas/ENGAGEMENT_SCHEMA.md` - canonical engagement documentation schema

**Decision recording:** When making governance decisions (structure, placement, patterns, chain changes), record a WS-DDR in `.context/DECISIONS.md` using DDR format. Read existing WS-DDRs before changing rules - they explain what not to break. Template: `Core/frameworks/intent/knowledge-engine/templates/ddr.md`.

## Domain Structure (Four Domains)

| Domain | Purpose | Entry Point |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| **Work/** | All professional activity - 4 pillars + Career | `Work/CONTEXT.md` |
| **Core/** | Reusable IP + products + external repos (see below) | `Core/CONTEXT.md` |
| **Personal/** | Individual life admin - financial, legal, hobbies, projects | `Personal/CONTEXT.md` |
| **Home/** | Real estate property management - TheParlor, TheFort | `Home/CONTEXT.md` |

### Work/ Pillars (Pipeline -> Execution in each)

| Pillar | Pipeline | Execution | Current Active |
|--------|----------|-----------|----------------|
| Consulting/ | Pipeline/ (prospects, proposals) | Engagements/ (one per client) | **Subaru** (primary), FidelityGuaranty |
| Advising/ | Pipeline/ (opportunities) | Engagements/ | - |
| Employment/ | Pipeline/ (applications, interviews) | Roles/ (one per company) | - |
| Lab/ | Pipeline/ (ideas, validation) | Ventures/ (active projects) | ConsultingOS |

Career/ sits at Work/ root as a cross-cutting narrative lens across all pillars.

## Engagement Directory Pattern (v4.0 - three zones)

Every engagement follows this flow:
- `from-client/` - VAULT: client originals, IMMUTABLE, never edit in place (copy to working/collaborative/ to collaborate)
- `working/` - HOT ZONE: drafts/, meetings/, notes/, collaborative/ (tolerates mess by design)
- `deliverables/` - FINISHED: shipped to client, date-prefixed when superseded
- `deliverables/archive/` - superseded versions

Plus standard optional: `financials/`, `proposals/`, `design/`, `onboarding/`, `reference/` (our research about client)
Plus KE optional (when Knowledge Farm exists): `knowledge/`, `raw/`

## File Naming Standard

`[Client]_[Program]_[Artifact_Name].[ext]` - program segment optional. Location signals lifecycle (working/ = draft, deliverables/ = final, archive/ = superseded). No `_DRAFT` or `_FINAL` suffixes.

## Brien's Preferences

- Visual thinker - diagrams, storytelling, analogies
- Engineer/architect/system designer mindset
- Product-first principles, design thinking
- Follows: Cagan, Patton, Herbig, Torres, Petra, Wagner, Seiden, Gothelf

## Vocabulary Standards

| NEVER Use | ALWAYS Use | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-----|
| Ceremonies | **Events** | Modern Scrum Guide language |
| Grooming | **Refinement** | Deprecated since 2013 |

## Core/ Three-Way Disambiguation (WS-DDR-016)

Core/ contains three distinct artifact types:

| Type | Path | What It Is |
|------|------|-----------|
| **Reusable IP** | `Core/frameworks/`, `Core/templates/`, `Core/reference/`, `Core/visuals/`, `Core/programs/` | Shareable consulting assets - any consultant could use |
| **Products** | `Core/products/` | Things Brien builds - 13 products under the Intent lifecycle. Forge is the composition engine (Methodology × Persona × Platform -> Deployed Skill). Cast is the persona engine, rendered by Forge. All 13 products live under `Core/products/` (WS-DDR-036, 2026-04-20). |
| **External** | `Core/external/` | Third-party repos Brien ingested - NOT Brien's IP |

**Products (alphabetical):** cast, cortege, digital-declutter, fieldbook, forge, library-index, library-index-mcp, loom, org-design-tooling, studio-control, topography, voices, witness.
_All 13 products live at `Core/products/`. intent-site is a framework satellite at `Core/frameworks/intent-site/`, not a product._

## Cross-Domain Awareness

| Working In | May Need Context From |
|------------|----------------------|
| Any engagement | `Core/frameworks/` for reusable IP |
| Work/Career | Engagement folders for proof points |
| Home/TheParlor | `Core/reference/materials/` for material specs |
| Any declutter | Full governance chain (above) |

## Autonomous Operations

Three autonomous agents run on schedule via launchd + Claude Code CLI.
Config lives in `Core/products/library-index/`:

| Agent | Schedule | Prompt | Digest |
|-------|----------|--------|--------|
| Library Index Nightly | 2:00 AM daily | `Core/products/library-index/.claude/commands/nightly-refresh.md` | `Core/products/library-index/logs/nightly-YYYY-MM-DD.json` |
| Workspace Health Check | 6:00 AM daily | `Core/products/library-index/.claude/commands/health-check.md` | `~/Workspaces/HEALTH_DIGEST.md` |
| Digital Declutter | TBD (Phase 3) | - | - |

### Health Check Dimensions

The health check scans 11 dimensions and writes `HEALTH_DIGEST.md` at the Workspaces root:

1. Stray files in home root
2. Scattered client content outside Workspaces
3. SESSION_HANDOFF freshness (<7 days)
4. Canonical structure (required directories exist)
5. Deprecated locations (should be deleted)
6. CATALOG coverage (>= 95%)
7. CONTEXT.md freshness (domain-level, <30 days)
8. Untagged files count (from CATALOG.json stats)
9. Git status (scripts repo - flag uncommitted changes)
10. Downloads folder size (>50 files triggers declutter)
11. PROPOSED_ENRICHMENTS backlog size

### Observability

- All agent sessions are captured by Entire.io (checkpoint branches in each repo)
- Structured JSON logs in `Core/products/library-index/logs/`
- launchd plists in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.brien.*`

## Session Protocols

See `.context/WORKSPACE_GOVERNANCE.md` for entry/intake/exit protocols.

id: SIG-UNATTENDED-CLAUDE-RUNS-NO-RETRY-ON-API-ERROR-2026-07-27
title: Two unattended launchd Claude runs died on transient API errors the same night, and neither retried
type: signal
kind: product-level-upgrade
status: open
severity: medium
created: 2026-07-27
discovered_by: weekly overwatch sweep (Sections 9d, 11c-exec)
scope: infrastructure
---

# Two scheduled runs failed the same night on transient API errors, and nothing retried either

## What happened

On the night of 2026-07-27, two independent unattended jobs both fired and both produced nothing:

- **Cast freshening nightly** (`com.brien.cast-freshening-nightly`). The log
  `Core/products/cast/engine/logs/launchd-freshening-2026-07-27.log` records `"is_error":true`
  with `terminal_reason: api_error` ("Connection closed mid-response") after 48 turns and roughly
  $4.86 of work. It never reached its `Freshen complete` marker. A cleanup step did run
  (`clean: 4 record(s), 0 violations`), so the job started fine and died mid-flight.
- **Governance audit** (`com.brien.governance-audit`). Neither `heartbeat-2026-07-27.txt` nor
  `governance-audit-2026-07-27.md` was written. The deadman check caught it and emitted
  `SIG-AUDIT-MISSING-2026-07-27` at 10:51Z.

Two jobs, same night, both dead. Anthropic status reported a brief Opus 5 elevated-error-rate
incident on 2026-07-27 (since resolved), which is a plausible common cause.

## Why this is a product-level upgrade and not just a bad night

The individual failures are transient and expected — API connections drop. The gap is that
**neither job has any retry**. A single transient blip converts directly into a missed day of
work, and the only reason anyone knows is that a separate second-observer script noticed the
absence after the fact.

The freshening case is the sharper one, because it defeats a detector. Overwatch Section 11c
checks whether each persona's *conclusion* is stale, and it read perfectly clean this sweep:
349 entries, 0 HIGH_RISK. That is not evidence of health. A run that produces nothing leaves
nothing for 11c to flag, so per-persona staleness checks are blind to executor death by
construction. Section 11c-exec exists precisely to cover that blind spot, and it is the only
reason the freshening failure surfaced at all.

So the detection layer is working. The **recovery** layer does not exist.

## What the upstream control would need to be

A retry-with-backoff wrapper around the `claude -p` invocation in the unattended launchd jobs,
distinguishing transient failure classes (`api_error`, connection closed mid-response, 429,
5xx) from genuine terminal failures (bad prompt, missing file, non-zero from the work itself).
Retrying a prompt error is waste; retrying a dropped socket is the whole point.

Two design constraints worth stating before anyone builds it:

1. **Retry must be budget-aware.** The freshening run had already spent ~$4.86 when it died. A
   naive 3x retry on a job that dies late is a 3x cost multiplier on the expensive tail. This
   matters more than usual right now: the same sweep measured weekly burn at 77% consumed
   against 41.8% of the week elapsed (1.84x ratio). A retry policy that ignores `codeburn`
   headroom would make a budget problem worse to fix a reliability problem.
2. **Retry must not silently mask a real regression.** If a job needs 3 attempts every night,
   that is a finding, not a success. Attempt count belongs in the log and in whatever the
   deadman reads, so "it eventually passed" never reads the same as "it passed."

## Candidate scope

- `Core/products/cast/engine/` freshening launchd entry point
- `Core/products/org-design-tooling/src/governance_heartbeat.sh` and the audit entry point
- Any other `claude -p` launchd job (the same pattern almost certainly repeats across the
  scheduled-task fleet; the quartermaster migration queue currently lists 8 plists)

## Closure DoD

- `upstream_control_path:` a shared retry wrapper used by the unattended `claude -p` jobs, not a
  one-off fix in the freshening script
- `catch_mechanism:` overwatch Section 11c-exec (already live for freshening) plus the governance
  deadman (already live for the audit) — both already proved they detect the failure; the new
  requirement is that attempt counts surface so retries do not hide degradation
- `pipeline_survival:` wrapper lives in the launchd invocation path, so it survives re-runs of the
  jobs themselves

## Related

- `SIG-AUDIT-MISSING-2026-07-27` (org-design-tooling) — the deadman's report of the audit half
- `Core/products/org-design-tooling/journal/JRN-20260727-overwatch-weekly-sweep.md` — the sweep
  that correlated the two failures

id: SIG-EVOLVES-SCAN-COUNTS-CENSUS-FILENAME-AS-CLAIM-2026-07-27
title: The evolves-not-deprecates scan flags a census data row as a deprecation claim
type: signal
kind: product-level-upgrade
status: open
severity: low

affects: Core/frameworks/intent-site/scripts/check-evolves-not-deprecates.sh

# The evolves-not-deprecates scan counts a filename inside a data table as a lifecycle claim

## What the scan reported

`check-evolves-not-deprecates.sh` exited 1 (DRIFT) on the 2026-07-27 sweep, with one offending
line:

```
Core/products/_intake/2026-07-19-signal-dirt-census/census.md:114
```

## Why it is a false positive

That line is a row in a census table. Its subject is a malformed YAML field: a `catch_mechanism`
value containing an unquoted colon-plus-space, which YAML's block-mapping parser misreads. The
row's finding column is about quoting the value. The string that triggered the matcher is the
*filename* in the row's first column, `SIG-EXEC-2026-06-05-ecosystem-deprecation-correction.md`,
which contains "deprecation" as part of a filename appearing in a data cell.

The line makes no claim about intent-site's lifecycle. It does not assert that intent-site is
deprecated, is being deprecated, or will be. Canon (SIG-INTENTSITE-2026-04-23, affirmed by
DEC-004) — intent-site evolves in place, full deprecation gates on Phase 3 — is not contradicted
anywhere in the scanned tree.

## The precision gap

The scan's rule is "intent-site coupled with an unqualified 'deprecat' claim in a descriptive
doc." It already excludes `.intent/` and frozen `archive/` eras, on the correct reasoning that
those legitimately quote the old stance as point-in-time fact. The same reasoning extends to
census and inventory artifacts: a document whose job is to *enumerate other files* will
mechanically reproduce their filenames, and those filenames are data, not assertions.

Right now the fix-suggestion the script prints ("add an evolves/gated qualifier to the line, or
move it under `.intent/`") is actively wrong for this case. Editing a census row to satisfy a
grep would corrupt the record — the row accurately describes a real file with a real YAML defect,

> **Owner:** Brien

## 1. Environment Path Equivalencies

The same filesystem appears at different mount points depending on how Claude accesses it.

| Environment | Root Path | How to Access |
|-------------|-----------|---------------|
| **macOS host** (Brien's laptop) | `/Users/brien/Workspaces/Core` | Finder, VS Code, Terminal |
| **Cowork session** (Read/Write/Edit tools) | `/Users/brien/Workspaces/Core` | Direct - same as host. Use this with Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep. |
| **Cowork bash** (mcp__workspace__bash) | `/sessions/*/mnt/Core/` | The session name changes each time. Discover it: `ls /sessions/*/mnt/Core/` |
| **Claude Code CLI** (local) | `/Users/brien/Workspaces/Core` | Same as host. `cd ~/Workspaces/Core` |
| **Claude Code CLI** (remote/headless) | Varies by mount | Check `pwd` and look for `Core/` in the path |

**Rule:** When writing file paths in documents, always use the macOS host path (`/Users/brien/Workspaces/Core/...`). Never embed session-specific bash mount paths in permanent files - they expire when the session ends.

**Cowork-specific note:** Cowork sessions start with NO folder mounted. Brien must select this folder (or Claude must call `request_cowork_directory` with path `/Users/brien/Workspaces/Core`). Once mounted, Read/Write/Edit hit the real filesystem. Files written here persist after the session ends.

### Portfolio taxonomy (WS-DDR-103)

`products/` holds **Engines** - the leaves of the **Composition** axis (build-scope): `Portfolio › Product Line › Product Suite/Group › Product`, where a *Product* is an atomic shippable engine (own repo, port, conservation law). Client **Engagements** are **not** products - they are **Instances** on the orthogonal **Instantiation** axis (run-scope: `Engine -> Instance`) and live under `Work/.../Engagements/<Client>/`, not here. Three cross-cutting overlays ride the tree without adding depth: **Surface** (how a product is accessed - CLI skill · MCP · Cowork · chat · scheduled task), **Bundle** (cross-*line* packaging), **Governance** (embedded self-monitoring, co-located with the governed). There is no canonical flat "product count" - engines are measured by Axis-1 placement. Canonical model: `Core/products/parallax/spec/2026-06-02-portfolio-taxonomy.md`.

- **CONTEXT.md:** Every directory should have one. Navigation index with parent/child/sibling links.
- **CLAUDE.md:** Product directories should have one. Operating conventions for that product.

# NOTICE: Governance at AI Creation Cadence

## Why this package exists

On 2026-07-24 Chris Markus forwarded a Boston Scientific req (Post Market AI Program Manager) with the note "they are still working on level and reporting." The first assessment priced it as a conventional CAPA governance role at $125 to $165/hr. Brien rejected that framing:

> "I think the fair market value is based on this being a typical CAPA governance role where knowledge of AI is not consequential to your ability to govern it. I think that might be missing the point that Intent sets out to address. If we can't create a work management system that can keep up with AI how could we possibly introduce compliance measures that can keep pace?"

He is correct, and the correction is bigger than one engagement. It names a category Brien has been building a reference implementation of for a year without positioning it: **governance and compliance instrumented to operate at the cadence at which AI authors and modifies systems, with the evidence generated as a byproduct rather than reconstructed after the fact.**

That thesis is not engagement-scoped. It is practice IP with at least three immediate consumers and a durable market anchor. It belongs in Core.

## The thesis in one paragraph

You cannot govern at human cadence a portfolio authored at machine cadence. When a quality organization can spin up forty AI-touched systems in a year and each one requires human-authored validation protocols, the compliance function becomes the binding constraint on the entire AI program, and most of the estate ends up ungoverned by construction. The finding an auditor writes is never "you moved too fast." It is **"you could not demonstrate control."** The fix is not more documentation produced faster. It is governance expressed as executable controls that emit continuous, provable evidence, which is precisely what FDA's Computer Software Assurance guidance asks for and what a Predetermined Change Control Plan presumes.

## Contents

| File | Covers |
|------|--------|
| design.md | The thesis, the Intent-to-QMS mapping spine, regulatory anchors, framing rules, disconfirmation pass, and the three consumer surfaces |
| STATUS.md | Disposition, open questions, promotion criteria |

## Why this is Core and not engagement-scoped

Per /Users/brien/Workspaces/AGENTS.md §2: another consultant could use this without modification. Nothing in it references Boston Scientific's internal data, org structure, or engagement context. The BSC-specific application lives at /Users/brien/Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/BostonScientific/ and the comp analysis at /Users/brien/Workspaces/Work/Career/getting-hired/working-docs/2026-07-24-ai-role-pathway-and-comp-assessment.md. This package holds only the transferable argument.

## What this package is not

It is not a product. It is not a methodology with a rendering pipeline. It is a positioning spine plus an evidence map. If it earns a paying instance and survives its disconfirmation pass, it promotes. Until then it is an intake topic with a live proof point.

## What happens next

1. The thesis feeds three surfaces immediately (see design.md §6): the reply to Chris, the scoped assessment SOW, and the first published piece.
2. Its central claim gets tested against a real regulated estate at Boston Scientific, or it does not, and the disconfirmation criteria in design.md §5 decide whether it holds.
3. Promotion criteria in STATUS.md.
