1	---
2	title: Governance at AI Creation Cadence - positioning spine
3	type: design
4	maturity: proposal
5	confidentiality: shareable
6	reusability: universal
7	created: 2026-07-24
8	domains:
9	  - ai-transformation
10	  - product-operating-models
11	frameworks:
12	  - intent
13	  - computer-software-assurance
14	  - predetermined-change-control-plan
15	purpose: The transferable argument, its evidence spine, its framing rules, its disconfirmation criteria, and its consumer surfaces.
16	---
17	
18	# Governance at AI Creation Cadence
19	
20	## 1. The argument
21	
22	**Premise 1.** AI has collapsed the cost of authoring and modifying systems. A single practitioner can now produce, in an afternoon, work that previously occupied a sprint team. Organizations experience this as an unplanned proliferation of AI-touched systems: forty ad hoc projects where there was a roadmap of six.
23	
24	**Premise 2.** Assurance did not get cheaper at the same rate. Validation protocols, change control, risk analysis, and effectiveness checks are still authored by humans, reviewed by humans, and evidenced in documents. Throughput is bounded by writer-hours.
25	
26	**Conclusion.** The assurance function becomes the binding constraint on the AI program. Two failure modes follow, and organizations pick one without noticing:
27	
28	- **Throttle.** Assurance holds the line, and the AI program moves at document cadence. The organization pays for capability it cannot deploy.
29	- **Leak.** The AI program routes around assurance, and the estate grows ungoverned. Nobody finds out until an inspection, an incident, or a recall.
30	
31	Most organizations are leaking and believe they are throttling.
32	
33	**The move.** Stop treating governance as documentation produced about a system, and start treating it as **executable controls that run inside the system and emit evidence continuously**. Provenance becomes a byproduct of doing the work rather than an artifact reconstructed afterward. Coverage stops being bounded by writer-hours and starts being bounded by instrumentation, which scales.
34	
35	## 2. The framing rule (load-bearing)
36	
37	**Never argue speed to an assurance audience.** In a regulated organization, and especially one under active remediation, "faster governance" is heard as "weaker governance" and the room is lost in one sentence.
38	
39	The same argument, correctly aimed:
40	
41	| Losing frame | Winning frame |
42	|---|---|
43	| Your compliance is too slow | You can only validate what a human can author a protocol for, so most of your estate is unevidenced |
44	| We need governance at AI speed | We need governance with AI-scale **coverage** |
45	| This accelerates approval | This makes control **demonstrable** on systems that currently have none |
46	| Less documentation | Documentation targeted where risk actually is, per CSA |
47	
48	Speed is a byproduct, never the pitch. The pitch is **coverage and provability**. An auditor never writes "you moved too fast." An auditor writes "you could not demonstrate control."
49	
50	## 3. Regulatory anchors
51	
52	The category does not need inventing. Two current pieces of FDA guidance already describe it, which converts the thesis from opinion into citation. (Medical device is the sharpest instance; the pattern generalizes to any regime with a validation obligation.)
53	
54	**Computer Software Assurance (CSA).** Final guidance issued 2025-09-24 by CDRH and CBER, updated 2026-02-03, following the 2022 draft. It moves industry away from exhaustive, one-size-fits-all documentation toward critical thinking and a risk-based, least-burdensome approach: assurance effort concentrated on functions that genuinely affect patient safety and product quality, with explicit endorsement of unscripted and exploratory testing, continuous monitoring, and leveraging supplier and developer evidence. Note the date: it landed one day after the QMSR framework took effect 2026-02-02. The regulator is actively telling industry to stop over-documenting and start testing what matters.
55	
56	**Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP).** Final guidance issued 2024-12-03, broadened from ML-only to all AI-enabled device software functions. It permits a system to keep changing after clearance without a new marketing submission per change, provided the plan describes the modifications, the methodology to develop, validate, and implement them, and an impact assessment. This is the sanctioned mechanism for "the governance keeps pace," with the agency's own name on it.
57	
58	**Scope discipline.** Production and quality system software (complaint triage, signal review, document workflow) sits under CSA and Part 11, not SaMD. CSA is the primary anchor for most enterprise AI estates. PCCP is the pattern to borrow for anything that will keep learning after it ships. Confusing the two is the fastest way to lose credibility with a quality audience.
59	
60	## 4. The evidence spine: Intent as a reference implementation
61	
62	The thesis is only credible because a working instance exists. Intent was not built as a compliance system, which is exactly what makes it useful: it is an unpremeditated, load-bearing instance of the pattern, running daily against real work.
63	
64	| Intent construct | Regulated-QMS equivalent | Why it transfers |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| Hooks (PreToolUse, Stop, SessionStart) | Automated controls | Enforced at the point of action, not asserted in a policy document. A blocked action is a control that demonstrably fired |
67	| Signals | Deviation and nonconformance capture | Recorded at point of occurrence by the actor, not reconstructed in a retrospective |
68	| Closure DoD (`upstream_control_path`, `catch_mechanism`, `pipeline_survival`) | CAPA effectiveness check | A machine-verifiable definition of "actually fixed" that distinguishes symptom repair from systemic control. This is precisely the FDA citation pattern: investigations scoped to the incident rather than the systemic root cause |
69	| chain_audit invariants | Continuous monitoring per CSA | Regression detection that runs on every pipeline pass rather than at annual review |
70	| Autonomy grants (L0 to L4) | Delegation of authority, segregation of duties | An explicit, testable statement of which decisions require which approver |
71	| Intent trace (notice to spec to execute to observe) | Design history and audit trail | Generated as a byproduct of doing the work rather than assembled for an auditor |
72	| Decision records (DDR) | Design review records with rationale | Rationale preserved at decision time, readable cold months later |
73	
74	**What this map is:** proof that the pattern runs, and knowledge of what breaks when it does.
75	
76	**What this map is not:** a product claim. Intent governs a single operator's workspace. It has never handled segregation of duties across teams, Part 11 electronic signatures, records retention schedules, auditor read access, or validation of the governance system itself. Overselling the transfer invites an architecture review that kills the engagement. The honest claim is a **reference implementation of the pattern plus scar tissue**, and that claim is both true and rare.
77	
78	## 5. Disconfirmation pass
79	
80	What would make this thesis wrong, and how it would be detected:
81	
82	| Claim | Falsifier | Detection |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| Assurance is the binding constraint | Organizations report AI portfolios stalled on data access, model quality, or funding rather than validation throughput | Ask three quality leaders what actually blocked their last AI deployment. If validation is not top-two, the premise is local, not general |
85	| Buyers feel the pain | Quality leaders describe their process as adequate and want more control, not different control | If the first conversation produces "we just need more validation engineers," the buyer is not ready and the sale is education, not delivery |
86	| Executable governance is transferable out of a solo context | The first multi-team instance collapses on segregation of duties, Part 11, or records retention | This is the highest-probability failure. It shows up in architecture review, not in the pitch. Treat it as the primary technical risk |
87	| The category is open | Deloitte, IQVIA, NAMSA, or a QMS vendor already sells this under a different name | Competitive scan before the first published piece. If a named practice exists, the position shifts from category creation to differentiated entry |
88	| Regulators tolerate it | CSA and PCCP get walked back, or inspectors in practice still demand traditional CSV artifacts | Watch inspection outcomes, not guidance text. Guidance permits; inspectors decide |
89	
90	**Honest standing:** the second row is the one most likely to bite first. A quality organization in active remediation defaults to more control, and this thesis has to be introduced as risk reduction through better evidence, never as relief from burden.
91	
92	## 6. Consumer surfaces
93	
94	One spine, three outputs, each a different altitude of the same argument.
95	
96	**6.1 Peer conversation (shortest).** No regulatory vocabulary, no pitch. Converts a headcount req into an engagement shape by naming the work that has to happen first. Reveals nothing about the thesis.
97	
98	**6.2 Scoped assessment SOW (middle).** Two halves. Half one is what the buyer asked for: portfolio rationalization, the combine, reuse, sequence, and kill calls with rationale, the overlap map across requirements, data sources, and technical capabilities. Half two is what the buyer needs: a CSA-aligned assurance approach for that estate, a PCCP-shaped change-control pattern for whatever will keep learning, and instrumentation that emits evidence continuously. **The assessment is itself the demo:** rationalizing a large estate in weeks with a machine-generated evidence trail, against an internal process that would take quarters and produce a deck, proves the argument without anyone having to make it. Sequencing rule: half two is revealed once the work is trusted, not in the opening.
99	
100	**6.3 Published piece (longest).** The thesis in public, with the CSA and PCCP anchors and the Intent mapping as the concrete instance. This is what makes a six-figure engagement legible to a buyer who has never met Brien, and it compounds with each delivered instance rather than competing with delivery for attention.
101	
102	## 7. Pricing implication
103	
104	This exits hourly, which is the point. A labor category is priced against a market of substitutes; a governance-system design with a working reference implementation has no substitute in a VMS catalog.
105	
106	| Shape | Range | Note |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| Conventional program-management framing | $125 to $165/hr | What the thesis is escaping |
109	| First engagement (reference-buying) | $50k to $70k, 4 to 6 weeks | Priced to acquire the logo and the case study |
110	| Standard engagement | $75k to $125k, 6 to 8 weeks | Once a delivered instance exists |
111	| Sustained program | $325 to $400/hr, or retainer per rate card S2 | If it becomes the estate standard |
112	
113	Rate card reference: /Users/brien/Workspaces/Core/reference/rate-card/rate-card-data.md. The blend is D4 (Product Taxonomy and Operating Models) plus D6 (AI Transformation and Enablement Advisory), with M1 multi-domain and M10 regulated vertical applying.
114	
115	## 8. Sources
116	
117	- [Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality System Software (FDA guidance)](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/computer-software-assurance-production-and-quality-system-software)
118	- [CSA final guidance availability notice (Federal Register, 2025-09-24)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/09/24/2025-18468/computer-software-assurance-for-production-and-quality-system-software-guidance-for-industry-and)
119	- [FDA Final Guidance: Computer Software Assurance (NSF)](https://www.nsf.org/life-science-regulatory-news/fda-final-guidance-computer-software-assurance-csa)

---
title: Governance at AI Creation Cadence - positioning spine
type: design
maturity: proposal
confidentiality: shareable
reusability: universal
created: 2026-07-24
domains:
  - ai-transformation
  - product-operating-models
frameworks:
  - intent
  - computer-software-assurance
  - predetermined-change-control-plan
purpose: The transferable argument, its evidence spine, its framing rules, its disconfirmation criteria, and its consumer surfaces.
---

# Governance at AI Creation Cadence

## 1. The argument

**Premise 1.** AI has collapsed the cost of authoring and modifying systems. A single practitioner can now produce, in an afternoon, work that previously occupied a sprint team. Organizations experience this as an unplanned proliferation of AI-touched systems: forty ad hoc projects where there was a roadmap of six.

**Premise 2.** Assurance did not get cheaper at the same rate. Validation protocols, change control, risk analysis, and effectiveness checks are still authored by humans, reviewed by humans, and evidenced in documents. Throughput is bounded by writer-hours.

**Conclusion.** The assurance function becomes the binding constraint on the AI program. Two failure modes follow, and organizations pick one without noticing:

- **Throttle.** Assurance holds the line, and the AI program moves at document cadence. The organization pays for capability it cannot deploy.
- **Leak.** The AI program routes around assurance, and the estate grows ungoverned. Nobody finds out until an inspection, an incident, or a recall.

Most organizations are leaking and believe they are throttling.

**The move.** Stop treating governance as documentation produced about a system, and start treating it as **executable controls that run inside the system and emit evidence continuously**. Provenance becomes a byproduct of doing the work rather than an artifact reconstructed afterward. Coverage stops being bounded by writer-hours and starts being bounded by instrumentation, which scales.

## 2. The framing rule (load-bearing)

**Never argue speed to an assurance audience.** In a regulated organization, and especially one under active remediation, "faster governance" is heard as "weaker governance" and the room is lost in one sentence.

The same argument, correctly aimed:

| Losing frame | Winning frame |
|---|---|
| Your compliance is too slow | You can only validate what a human can author a protocol for, so most of your estate is unevidenced |
| We need governance at AI speed | We need governance with AI-scale **coverage** |
| This accelerates approval | This makes control **demonstrable** on systems that currently have none |
| Less documentation | Documentation targeted where risk actually is, per CSA |

Speed is a byproduct, never the pitch. The pitch is **coverage and provability**. An auditor never writes "you moved too fast." An auditor writes "you could not demonstrate control."

## 3. Regulatory anchors

The category does not need inventing. Two current pieces of FDA guidance already describe it, which converts the thesis from opinion into citation. (Medical device is the sharpest instance; the pattern generalizes to any regime with a validation obligation.)

**Computer Software Assurance (CSA).** Final guidance issued 2025-09-24 by CDRH and CBER, updated 2026-02-03, following the 2022 draft. It moves industry away from exhaustive, one-size-fits-all documentation toward critical thinking and a risk-based, least-burdensome approach: assurance effort concentrated on functions that genuinely affect patient safety and product quality, with explicit endorsement of unscripted and exploratory testing, continuous monitoring, and leveraging supplier and developer evidence. Note the date: it landed one day after the QMSR framework took effect 2026-02-02. The regulator is actively telling industry to stop over-documenting and start testing what matters.

**Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP).** Final guidance issued 2024-12-03, broadened from ML-only to all AI-enabled device software functions. It permits a system to keep changing after clearance without a new marketing submission per change, provided the plan describes the modifications, the methodology to develop, validate, and implement them, and an impact assessment. This is the sanctioned mechanism for "the governance keeps pace," with the agency's own name on it.

**Scope discipline.** Production and quality system software (complaint triage, signal review, document workflow) sits under CSA and Part 11, not SaMD. CSA is the primary anchor for most enterprise AI estates. PCCP is the pattern to borrow for anything that will keep learning after it ships. Confusing the two is the fastest way to lose credibility with a quality audience.

## 4. The evidence spine: Intent as a reference implementation

The thesis is only credible because a working instance exists. Intent was not built as a compliance system, which is exactly what makes it useful: it is an unpremeditated, load-bearing instance of the pattern, running daily against real work.

| Intent construct | Regulated-QMS equivalent | Why it transfers |
|---|---|---|
| Hooks (PreToolUse, Stop, SessionStart) | Automated controls | Enforced at the point of action, not asserted in a policy document. A blocked action is a control that demonstrably fired |
| Signals | Deviation and nonconformance capture | Recorded at point of occurrence by the actor, not reconstructed in a retrospective |
| Closure DoD (`upstream_control_path`, `catch_mechanism`, `pipeline_survival`) | CAPA effectiveness check | A machine-verifiable definition of "actually fixed" that distinguishes symptom repair from systemic control. This is precisely the FDA citation pattern: investigations scoped to the incident rather than the systemic root cause |
| chain_audit invariants | Continuous monitoring per CSA | Regression detection that runs on every pipeline pass rather than at annual review |
| Autonomy grants (L0 to L4) | Delegation of authority, segregation of duties | An explicit, testable statement of which decisions require which approver |
| Intent trace (notice to spec to execute to observe) | Design history and audit trail | Generated as a byproduct of doing the work rather than assembled for an auditor |
| Decision records (DDR) | Design review records with rationale | Rationale preserved at decision time, readable cold months later |

**What this map is:** proof that the pattern runs, and knowledge of what breaks when it does.

**What this map is not:** a product claim. Intent governs a single operator's workspace. It has never handled segregation of duties across teams, Part 11 electronic signatures, records retention schedules, auditor read access, or validation of the governance system itself. Overselling the transfer invites an architecture review that kills the engagement. The honest claim is a **reference implementation of the pattern plus scar tissue**, and that claim is both true and rare.

## 5. Disconfirmation pass

What would make this thesis wrong, and how it would be detected:

| Claim | Falsifier | Detection |
|---|---|---|
| Assurance is the binding constraint | Organizations report AI portfolios stalled on data access, model quality, or funding rather than validation throughput | Ask three quality leaders what actually blocked their last AI deployment. If validation is not top-two, the premise is local, not general |
| Buyers feel the pain | Quality leaders describe their process as adequate and want more control, not different control | If the first conversation produces "we just need more validation engineers," the buyer is not ready and the sale is education, not delivery |
| Executable governance is transferable out of a solo context | The first multi-team instance collapses on segregation of duties, Part 11, or records retention | This is the highest-probability failure. It shows up in architecture review, not in the pitch. Treat it as the primary technical risk |
| The category is open | Deloitte, IQVIA, NAMSA, or a QMS vendor already sells this under a different name | Competitive scan before the first published piece. If a named practice exists, the position shifts from category creation to differentiated entry |
| Regulators tolerate it | CSA and PCCP get walked back, or inspectors in practice still demand traditional CSV artifacts | Watch inspection outcomes, not guidance text. Guidance permits; inspectors decide |

**Honest standing:** the second row is the one most likely to bite first. A quality organization in active remediation defaults to more control, and this thesis has to be introduced as risk reduction through better evidence, never as relief from burden.

## 6. Consumer surfaces

One spine, three outputs, each a different altitude of the same argument.

**6.1 Peer conversation (shortest).** No regulatory vocabulary, no pitch. Converts a headcount req into an engagement shape by naming the work that has to happen first. Reveals nothing about the thesis.

**6.2 Scoped assessment SOW (middle).** Two halves. Half one is what the buyer asked for: portfolio rationalization, the combine, reuse, sequence, and kill calls with rationale, the overlap map across requirements, data sources, and technical capabilities. Half two is what the buyer needs: a CSA-aligned assurance approach for that estate, a PCCP-shaped change-control pattern for whatever will keep learning, and instrumentation that emits evidence continuously. **The assessment is itself the demo:** rationalizing a large estate in weeks with a machine-generated evidence trail, against an internal process that would take quarters and produce a deck, proves the argument without anyone having to make it. Sequencing rule: half two is revealed once the work is trusted, not in the opening.

**6.3 Published piece (longest).** The thesis in public, with the CSA and PCCP anchors and the Intent mapping as the concrete instance. This is what makes a six-figure engagement legible to a buyer who has never met Brien, and it compounds with each delivered instance rather than competing with delivery for attention.

## 7. Pricing implication

This exits hourly, which is the point. A labor category is priced against a market of substitutes; a governance-system design with a working reference implementation has no substitute in a VMS catalog.

| Shape | Range | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional program-management framing | $125 to $165/hr | What the thesis is escaping |
| First engagement (reference-buying) | $50k to $70k, 4 to 6 weeks | Priced to acquire the logo and the case study |
| Standard engagement | $75k to $125k, 6 to 8 weeks | Once a delivered instance exists |
| Sustained program | $325 to $400/hr, or retainer per rate card S2 | If it becomes the estate standard |

Rate card reference: /Users/brien/Workspaces/Core/reference/rate-card/rate-card-data.md. The blend is D4 (Product Taxonomy and Operating Models) plus D6 (AI Transformation and Enablement Advisory), with M1 multi-domain and M10 regulated vertical applying.

# Applied-AI resume and LinkedIn language

## The finding that should drive all of this

The credential gap is not that no title on Brien's record says AI. That framing, from
/Users/brien/Workspaces/Work/Consulting/Engagements/BostonScientific/ENGAGEMENT_INDEX.md,
is true but it points at the wrong fix. It implies he needs to go acquire the credential.

He already did the work. It is filed under other names.

**Butterfly Network, Nov 2022 to Jul 2023, accomplishment 4** in
/Users/brien/Workspaces/Work/Career/getting-hired/working-docs/COMPLETE_CAREER_INVENTORY_CONSOLIDATED_v3.md:

> "Strategized multi-app experience publishing to streamline feature releases **and AI models**
> across **regulatory and non-regulatory paths**."

That is AI release governance inside an FDA-regulated medical device company. It is the single
most relevant sentence in a thirty-year inventory for the Boston Scientific req, and it currently
appears nowhere on the LinkedIn profile, nowhere in the headline, and nowhere in the About
section. It is item 4 of 6 under a role that displays as "9 months."

So the move is not to manufacture AI credibility. It is to stop burying it.

Three assets, in descending order of how much work they do:

1. **Butterfly.** FDA-regulated medical devices, AI model release paths, regulatory and
   non-regulatory routing. Directly on-target and currently invisible.
2. **The governance-at-AI-cadence thesis.** Brien's own current positioning, written 2026-07-24,
   at /Users/brien/Workspaces/Core/products/_intake/2026-07-24-ai-cadence-governance-thesis/design.md
   with CSA and PCCP anchors and Intent as a working reference implementation.
3. **Thirty years of portfolio and operating-model work.** The rationalization mandate in the BSC
   req (combine, reuse, sequence, pause) is portfolio taxonomy work he has done repeatedly at
   scale, including a 38-product enablement portfolio design.

## The framing rule, carried over

From design.md section 2, and it governs every line below:

**Never argue speed to an assurance audience.** "Faster governance" is heard as "weaker
governance" and the room is lost in one sentence. The pitch is **coverage and provability**. An
auditor never writes "you moved too fast." An auditor writes "you could not demonstrate control."

This is why none of the copy below says "accelerate," "at AI speed," "move faster," or
"streamline compliance." Every claim is aimed at coverage, evidence, and demonstrable control.

---

## 1. LinkedIn headline

**Current (live):**

```
I design environments where product teams thrive | Transformation Architect | Systems thinker, Builder, Operator | 30+ years in product, engineering & operations
```

It is a good headline for the practice Brien had. It does zero work for an AI-governance buyer,
and headline is the highest-weight field in recruiter search.

**Recommended replacement:**

```
I make AI portfolios governable | Applied-AI governance in regulated environments | Transformation Architect | 30+ years product, engineering & operations
```

139 characters of 220.

Why this one: "governable" is the buyer's word, not the seller's. It says the object is a
portfolio (which is what the BSC req governs) rather than a model. "Regulated" carries the
premium and filters out the wrong inbound. The back half preserves the existing equity so the
profile does not read as a pivot by someone with nothing behind it.

## Status

## The driver, confirmed

**Four concurrent post-market actions**, two of them at Class I severity, both in cardiac rhythm management (the Arden Hills franchise):

- **ACCOLADE pacemakers:** FDA Class I recall correction 2026-03-18 (203,000 devices, 4 deaths, 2,557 serious injuries), expanded by a 2026-05-08 advisory to **1.3 million devices**.

**Precedent that explains "driven at the highest":** BSC took a **corporate warning letter in January 2006** citing "patchy review, analysis, and reporting of product complaints, including products that had been recalled." That is the Guardian problem statement twenty years early. content.text:
## Findings: Butterfly Network customer/deployment scale, Nov 2022–Jul 2023

I checked SEC EDGAR (full-text search across every Butterfly Network filing, all years, not just the window) and the company's own earnings press releases and earnings-call transcripts from Q4 2022 through Q2 2023. Bottom line: **neither claim appears verbatim in any primary source, and the strongest related SEC-filed figure actively caps out below "120."**

### 1. "120+ hospital organizations" — CONTRADICTED (by the closest available figure) / phrase never used

- **SEC EDGAR full-text search for the phrases "120 hospital," "120 health system," "120+ hospital," "more than 120 hospital," "over 120 health," and "hospital organizations" all return zero hits** — across every Butterfly Network filing ever made (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1/S-3, POS AM, 424B3, proxy), not just the Nov 2022–Jul 2023 window. Query tool: `efts.sec.gov` full-text search scoped to CIK 0001804176. This means "120" in this framing is not a number the company itself has ever put in an SEC filing.
- What the company **did** say, verbatim, in the **FY2022 10-K** (filed 2023-03-23, covering fiscal year ended 2022-12-31 — squarely in-window): 
  > "In the United States, Butterfly has been purchased by a clinician in most of the largest 100 healthcare systems."
  Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000155837023004464/bfly-20221231x10k.htm (Business section)
- This is a materially different and weaker claim than "120+ hospital organizations" in two ways: (a) it caps the universe at the **largest 100** health systems, not 120+; (b) it says "purchased by **a clinician**" (i.e., at least one individual buyer inside that system), not that the system itself is an institutional/enterprise customer. That's a much thinner bar than "hospital organizations" as customers.
- I traced this exact sentence and found it is **static boilerplate**: it appears word-for-word in the FY2021 10-K (filed 2022-02-28), the FY2021 10-K/A (2022-03-28), the FY2022 10-K (2023-03-23, in-window), two POS AM prospectuses (2023-05-02 and 2023-08-08, both boundary-adjacent to the window), and even the FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-03-04) — the company never updated this number over three annual reports. So even if a resume-writer were reading loosely, the ceiling this specific SEC disclosure supports is "100," not "120+," and it never moved.
- Earnings-call transcripts (Q4 2022 call, 2023-02-28; Q1 2023 call, 2023-05-11; Q2 2023 call, ~2023-08-03) describe specific named deployments (Hennepin County, University Hospital Bonn, University of Rochester Medical Center, Mayo, Stanford, UCLA, Denver Health, University of Maryland, a Minnesota rural-hospital rollout "to over 100 rural and critical access hospitals throughout the state" via a third-party grantee HQ Med Ed) but **never give an aggregate hospital/health-system customer count** — no "we now have X hospital customers" statement anywhere in this window.

**Verdict: the "100 healthcare systems" SEC language is the closest primary-sourced figure, and it is lower than and differently defined than "120+ hospital organizations." I would call this CONTRADICTED as a numeric claim, not merely silent — the company's own ceiling was 100, worded as "purchased by a clinician in," which is not equivalent to "120+ hospital organizations" as customers.**

### 2. "Tens of thousands of clinicians" — PARTIALLY CORROBORATED, with a wording caveat

- **Q4 2022 earnings press release** (8-K Exhibit 99.1, filed 2023-02-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000155837023002249/bfly-20230228xex99d1.htm), quote from Founder/Chairman/Interim CEO Jonathan Rothberg, verbatim:
  > "our solution has touched the lives of millions of patients and is being used by tens of thousands of practitioners across the globe each and every day"
  This is repeated near-verbatim on the Q4 2022 earnings call (same date).
- This says **"practitioners," not "clinicians."** They're close in meaning but not identical terms, and if a resume claim asserts "clinicians" as if it were the company's own word, that's a paraphrase, not a verbatim citation. I'd flag this distinction as material if defensibility of exact phrasing matters.
- No SEC filing (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) uses "tens of thousands of clinicians" verbatim — full-text search returned zero hits for that exact phrase, ever.
- Related but distinct scale figures found in-window, all clearly labeled by what they actually measure (not clinicians/customers):
  - **"more than 80,000 Butterfly iQ and Butterfly iQ+ devices" sold and shipped** — FY2022 10-K, as of 2023-03-23 filing (period ended 2022-12-31). This is a device/unit count, not a clinician or hospital count.
  - **"nearly 100,000 ultrasound probes shipped"** — Q1 2023 earnings call, 2023-05-11 (device count, cumulative).
  - **"100,000 units out in the marketplace and growing"** — Q2 2023 earnings call, ~2023-08-03 (device count; also just past your Jul 2023 cutoff — flagging as boundary-adjacent, not squarely in-window).
  - **"nearly 15,000 users have accessed our Butterfly Academy courses"** — Q2 2023 earnings call, ~2023-08-03 (Academy training-platform signups specifically, not total clinician users of the device; also boundary-adjacent to your window, and 15,000 falls short of "tens of thousands" on its own).

**Verdict: "tens of thousands of practitioners" (not "clinicians") is a genuine, verbatim, primary-sourced, in-window (Feb 2023) claim from Butterfly Network's own CEO in an SEC-filed press release. It CORROBORATES the substance of "tens of thousands of clinicians" but not the exact word choice.**

### What I could not find
- No primary source (SEC filing, earnings release, or earnings call transcript, Nov 2022–Jul 2023) states an aggregate count of hospital/health-system customers using the term "hospital organizations," at any number, let alone 120+.
- No 10-Q (Q1/Q2/Q3 2023) contains customer-count or hospital-count language at all — that disclosure only lives in the annual 10-K's Business section, and it says "100," unchanged, for three years running.
- I did not find any reputable press coverage (BusinessWire, PRNewswire, trade press) from the window citing a "120" figure in any framing. Searches for "120 hospital," "120+ hospital," "120 health system" tied to Butterfly Network returned nothing relevant in any year, including outside the window (2024–2025 coverage doesn't have it either).

import re
p='LINKEDIN_EXPERIENCE_REWRITE.md'

def head_fix(m):

s=re.sub(r'^#{1,6} .*$', head_fix, s, flags=re.M)

# Intent — Development Continuity Guide

> This file exists so that any AI agent or human contributor can pick up Intent development without prior session context. Read this first.

## ⚠ CRITICAL: This Repo Contains Two Products

**Read this first. This is the most common source of session drift.**

This repo contains **two distinct products** that share a repo but have different purposes, different users, and different development paths:

### 1. Intent (Methodology)
An operating model for AI-augmented product teams. **Notice → Spec → Execute → Observe.** Domain-agnostic. Replaces Agile ceremony overhead. Lives in: `spec/`, `.intent/`, `bin/`, `servers/`.

### 2. Knowledge Engine (Product)
A compiled knowledge base system: `raw/` sources → agent-compiled `knowledge/` artifacts → ingest/query/lint operations. Separable from Intent — can be used without the loop. Lives in: `knowledge-engine/` (AGENTS.md, specs, templates).

### 3. Knowledge Farm (Instance — not in this repo)
A specific deployment of the Knowledge Engine for a domain. Brien's Knowledge Farm is his consulting practice first-brain (Subaru, ASA, F&G engagements). It spans `Core/` and `Work/Consulting/Engagements/*/`. Brien's farm feeds Intent ONLY because his domain (product strategy) overlaps with Intent's domain — **this is coincidental, not structural.**

### How to tell which product you're working on

| If you're touching... | You're in... |
|----------------------|-------------|
| The loop, trust scoring, work ontology, signals, intents | **Intent** (methodology) |
| AGENTS.md, ingest/query/lint, federation, enrichment, redaction | **Knowledge Engine** (product) |
| Subaru/ASA/F&G engagement data, Brien's engagement knowledge | **Brien's Knowledge Farm** (instance) |

### Decided Architecture (2026-04-06)

| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| Knowledge Engine MCP server | New `intent-knowledge` server (port 8004), separate from notice/spec/observe |
| Knowledge Engine CLI | New `intent-knowledge` tool (subcommands: ingest, query, lint) |
| Retroactive enrichment trigger | Suggested-first (lint detects opportunity, surfaces signal), on-demand second |
| Engagement rollout order | Subaru → F&G → ASA → Cargill → Footlocker |
| Redaction enforcement | Tool-level (MCP server applies projection automatically) |

---

## What Is Intent?

Intent is a **team operating model for AI-augmented product teams**. It replaces Agile's ceremony-driven coordination with a continuous loop: **Notice → Spec → Execute → Observe**. When AI collapses implementation from weeks to hours, the bottleneck moves upstream — from delivery to discovery, specification, and observation. Intent is the operating model for that new reality.

Intent is NOT a SaaS tool (yet). It's a methodology that lives in files, tracked in git, observable through events. Teams adopt it by adding a `.intent/` directory to their repos.

### Three-Layer Architecture (v1.0 — 2026-04-05)

Intent's methodology prescribes three layers that work together:

| Layer | Purpose | Directories | Analogy |
|-------|---------|-------------|---------|
| **1. Compiled Knowledge Base** | Everything the system knows about the problem domain | `raw/`, `knowledge/` | The Knowledge Engine product provides this |
| **2. Transformation OS** | The notice→spec→execute→observe engine. Domain-agnostic. | `.intent/`, `spec/` (methodology) | Intent methodology |
| **3. Software Spec & Code** | Specs, contracts, and running code | `spec/` (generated), `src/` | The output |

**Six bidirectional data flows couple the layers:**
1. Knowledge → Notice: Lint surfaces signals (gaps, contradictions, staleness)
2. Notice → Spec (via knowledge): Spec authoring queries knowledge base for personas, journeys, DDRs
3. Spec → Execute: Trust-gated agents build against specs
4. Execute → Observe: Running code emits events
5. **Observe → Knowledge (double-loop):** Observations update domain models — questioning assumptions, not just optimizing
6. Observe → Spec corpus (single-loop): Spec drift detection, living doc sync

**Knowledge Engine schema:** `knowledge-engine/AGENTS.md`
**Knowledge Engine specs:** `knowledge-engine/spec/` (operations, federation, enrichment, redaction, boundary)
**Research archive:** `reference/karpathy-synthesis/`

**Owner:** Brien (theparlorhq@gmail.com) — solo practitioner, The Parlor
**Repo:** github.com/theparlor/intent (private)
**Site repo:** github.com/theparlor/intent-site → https://theparlor.github.io/intent-site/
**Status:** Methodology defined, CLI suite + MCP server operational, signal dashboard live, trust framework specced, signal management CLI operational (review/dismiss/cluster/promote). All 13 founding signals scored with trust levels.

## Core Concepts

### The Loop
```
NOTICE  →  SPEC  →  EXECUTE  →  OBSERVE  →  (back to NOTICE)
```
No sprint boundaries. No ceremony tax. A continuous loop where the team's energy follows the highest-leverage work.

### Four Products
Intent is four products, not one. Each phase of the loop is a product with its own maturity:
- **Notice** (Operational) — Signal capture from any surface. MCP server, CLI, GitHub Action built.
- **Spec** (Conceptual) — Shaping signals into agent-ready specs. Templates, CLI tools built.
- **Execute** (Defined) — Agent implementation against specs. Event schema defined, no integration yet.
- **Observe** (Schema-Ready) — Dashboard and learning layer. 15 event types defined, no visualization yet.

See `spec/product-roadmap.md` for the full four-product roadmap with investments.

### Work Ontology (7 levels)
Signal → Intent → Spec → Contract → Capability → Feature → Product

Each level has a clear owner, clear transitions, and clear events. This replaces stories, epics, and backlogs.

### Four Personas
- **△ Practitioner-Architect** (amber) — Senior ICs, system thinkers. Primary: Notice, Spec.
- **◇ Product-Minded Leader** (blue) — PMs, business context. Primary: Notice, Observe.
- **○ Design-Quality Advocate** (purple) — Designers/QA, contract quality. Primary: Spec, Observe.
- **◉ AI Agent** (green) — Claude Code, GitHub Actions. Primary: Execute, Observe.
  - **Authoring Provenance Sources:** Entire.io session traces, Granola transcripts, session-ledger md (feed Notice and Observe as event sources, not as agents).

### Event System
15 OTel-compatible events across 6 emission mechanisms. Events stored in `.intent/events/events.jsonl`. Schema: version, event, timestamp, trace_id (=Intent), span_id (=work unit), parent_id (=hierarchy), source, data.

### Three-Layer Repo Pattern (Extended)
- `raw/` — Immutable source material (research, analytics, competitors, support). LLM reads, never writes.
- `knowledge/` — LLM-compiled domain knowledge (personas, journeys, DDRs, themes, domain models, rationale). Agent writes, human reviews.
- `.intent/` — Work artifacts (signals, intents, specs, contracts, decisions, events, templates)
- `observations/` — Runtime feedback (metrics, incidents) that feeds back into knowledge base and specs
- `.claude/` — Agent reasoning (project context, session transcripts)
- `.entire/` — Authoring provenance (agent-session traces from Entire.io). One source feeding `.intent/events/events.jsonl`.

### Signal Capture System
A 5-tier adapter architecture for capturing signals from every surface where practitioners work:
1. **MCP Server** (Tier 1) — Claude Code, Cowork, Cursor. 7 tools: signal capture/list/get, intent propose, spec create, status.
2. **CLI** (Tier 2) — `bin/intent-signal`, `bin/intent-intent`, `bin/intent-spec`, `bin/intent-status`. Full suite.
3. **Slack** (Tier 3) — Reaction-based or slash command. Specced, not built.
4. **GitHub** (Tier 4) — Issue labels, PR comments. Specced, not built.
5. **AI Plugins** (Tier 5) — ChatGPT, Copilot, Codex. Specced, not built.

See `spec/signal-capture-system.md` for the full architecture.

### Signal Trust & Autonomous Execution

Signals are not just captured — they are enriched, scored, classified, and routed through an autonomous processing pipeline. The goal: work every signal as far along as it can go, with humans intervening only when something is unsafe or too ambiguous.

**Trust Model:** Every signal gets two scores:
- **Confidence** (0-1): How likely is this signal real and worth acting on?
- **Trust** (0-1): How confidently can an agent resolve this without human input?

Trust = clarity × 0.30 + (1/blast_radius) × 0.20 + reversibility × 0.20 + testability × 0.20 + precedent × 0.10

**Autonomy Levels:**
- L0 (trust < 0.2): Human drives — strategic, ambiguous
- L1 (0.2–0.4): Agent assists — enriches, human decides
- L2 (0.4–0.6): Agent decides, human approves — drafts intent+spec
- L3 (0.6–0.85): Agent executes, human monitors — full loop, observe after
- L4 (≥ 0.85): Full autonomy — circuit breakers only

**L0 Approval Gate (SPEC-APPROVAL-GATE):** External communication (Slack, email, PR, calendar) is governed by a typed approval protocol, not just prompt adherence. The gate intercepts L0 actions, constructs IntentApproval entities, and blocks until Brien decides. Configuration source of truth: `.intent/config/approval-rules.yml`. Methodology: `methodology/meta/approval-gate.md`. Gate skill: `platforms/claude-code/governance/intent-approval-gate/SKILL.md`.

**Three Human-Contact Patterns:**
- Phase gates (Notice→Spec): mandatory, prevents building the wrong thing
- Action gates (L0 approval): mandatory, prevents saying the wrong thing
- Strategic requests (`request_human_input`): voluntary, agent-initiated at any trust level

All three use the shared `execution.paused` / `execution.resumed` checkpoint protocol.

**Enrichment Pipeline:** Source Adapter → Dedup Agent → Context Agent → Trust Scorer → Classifier → Router

**Disambiguation Loop:** When an agent hits ambiguity, it generates a new signal asking a better question. The system never dead-ends.

See `spec/signal-trust-framework.md` for the full architecture.

### Deployment Topology

Intent supports a config-driven deployment model. The same tools work in two modes:

**Local mode:** `.intent/` in git is the source of truth. CLI tools read/write files. MCP server reads/writes files. Signal dashboard reads from git. Best for solo practitioners and teams that want full git control.

**Hosted mode (planned):** A service is the source of truth. CLI and MCP become API clients. Dashboard reads from the service. `.intent/` in git becomes an optional sync target. Required for always-on agent processing (Brien's laptop goes offline during travel).

Configuration lives in `.intent/config.yml` (schema in `spec/signal-trust-framework.md`). The same CLI commands, MCP tools, and dashboard work in both modes — only the backend changes.

The processing pipeline (enrichment agents, routing, execution) must run somewhere always-on. Options under evaluation: GitHub Actions (simplest), cloud service (most capable), dedicated machine (interim).

## CLI Suite

All CLI tools share the same architecture: walk up from `$PWD` to find `.intent/`, generate sequential IDs, write markdown with YAML frontmatter, emit events to `events.jsonl`, optional `--commit` flag.

### intent-signal
```bash

intent-signal "Title" --confidence 0.8 --trust 0.6  # With scores (auto-computes autonomy level)
intent-signal "Title" --source pr-review             # With source attribution

# Triage

intent-signal review SIG-003                         # Review a specific signal

# Lifecycle

intent-signal cluster SIG-001,SIG-003 --name "Group" # Group related signals
intent-signal promote SIG-003                        # Promote signal → intent

# Query
intent-signal list                                   # List active signals
intent-signal list --status captured                 # Filter by status
intent-signal list --all                             # Include dismissed
intent-signal show SIG-003                           # Show full signal file
```

### intent-intent

intent-intent accept INT-003                                  # Accept for shaping
```

### intent-spec

```

### intent-status

## Key Decisions (for context)

File placement within Workspaces governed by [/Workspaces/AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) — the authoritative placement resolver. Intent-specific knowledge artifacts follow the federation model in `knowledge-engine/spec/federation.md`.

> **Chainable atoms:** These 21 decisions are also represented as decision atoms in `.intent/decisions/DEC-INTENT-001.md` through `DEC-INTENT-021.md` for full chainability. The prose below is the human-readable summary; the atoms are the machine-traversable form. Both forms are authoritative — do not delete the prose.

1. **Named "Intent"** — not "Dev OS", Frame, Premise, or Lucid. The name IS the thing.
2. **Methodology first, tool second** — validate with practitioners before building software.
3. **Open development** — signals, decisions, architecture all public. Dogfood the observe layer.
4. **File-native, git-tracked, OTel-compatible** — no lock-in, no proprietary formats.
5. **Target practitioner-architects first** — senior ICs who feel the gap and have org influence.
6. **Specs as contracts, not stories** — agents need verifiable assertions, not prose.
7. **Staged GTM** — thought leadership → methodology product → tooling (conditional).
8. **Four-product framing** — Notice, Spec, Execute, Observe are distinct products with own roadmaps.
9. **Three-layer architecture** — Compiled knowledge base (Karpathy pattern) + Transformation OS (Intent loop) + Software Spec/Code. Independent layers, bidirectionally coupled. (2026-04-05)
10. **Compilation over retrieval** — The knowledge base compiles understanding once and keeps it current. Not RAG. Cross-references already there. Contradictions already flagged.
11. **Double-loop learning** — Observe updates Layer 1 (domain understanding), not just Layer 3 (execution). Without this, system can only optimize, never question. (Argyris)

# Intent — Development Continuity Guide

> This file exists so that any AI agent or human contributor can pick up Intent development without prior session context. Read this first.

## ⚠ CRITICAL: This Repo Contains Two Products

**Read this first. This is the most common source of session drift.**

This repo contains **two distinct products** that share a repo but have different purposes, different users, and different development paths:

### 1. Intent (Methodology)
An operating model for AI-augmented product teams. **Notice → Spec → Execute → Observe.** Domain-agnostic. Replaces Agile ceremony overhead. Lives in: `spec/`, `.intent/`, `bin/`, `servers/`.

### 2. Knowledge Engine (Product)
A compiled knowledge base system: `raw/` sources → agent-compiled `knowledge/` artifacts → ingest/query/lint operations. Separable from Intent — can be used without the loop. Lives in: `knowledge-engine/` (AGENTS.md, specs, templates).

### 3. Knowledge Farm (Instance — not in this repo)
A specific deployment of the Knowledge Engine for a domain. Brien's Knowledge Farm is his consulting practice first-brain (Subaru, ASA, F&G engagements). It spans `Core/` and `Work/Consulting/Engagements/*/`. Brien's farm feeds Intent ONLY because his domain (product strategy) overlaps with Intent's domain — **this is coincidental, not structural.**

### How to tell which product you're working on

| If you're touching... | You're in... |
|----------------------|-------------|
| The loop, trust scoring, work ontology, signals, intents | **Intent** (methodology) |
| AGENTS.md, ingest/query/lint, federation, enrichment, redaction | **Knowledge Engine** (product) |
| Subaru/ASA/F&G engagement data, Brien's engagement knowledge | **Brien's Knowledge Farm** (instance) |

### Decided Architecture (2026-04-06)

| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| Knowledge Engine MCP server | New `intent-knowledge` server (port 8004), separate from notice/spec/observe |
| Knowledge Engine CLI | New `intent-knowledge` tool (subcommands: ingest, query, lint) |
| Retroactive enrichment trigger | Suggested-first (lint detects opportunity, surfaces signal), on-demand second |
| Engagement rollout order | Subaru → F&G → ASA → Cargill → Footlocker |
| Redaction enforcement | Tool-level (MCP server applies projection automatically) |

---

## What Is Intent?

Intent is a **team operating model for AI-augmented product teams**. It replaces Agile's ceremony-driven coordination with a continuous loop: **Notice → Spec → Execute → Observe**. When AI collapses implementation from weeks to hours, the bottleneck moves upstream — from delivery to discovery, specification, and observation. Intent is the operating model for that new reality.

Intent is NOT a SaaS tool (yet). It's a methodology that lives in files, tracked in git, observable through events. Teams adopt it by adding a `.intent/` directory to their repos.

### Three-Layer Architecture (v1.0 — 2026-04-05)

Intent's methodology prescribes three layers that work together:

| Layer | Purpose | Directories | Analogy |
|-------|---------|-------------|---------|
| **1. Compiled Knowledge Base** | Everything the system knows about the problem domain | `raw/`, `knowledge/` | The Knowledge Engine product provides this |
| **2. Transformation OS** | The notice→spec→execute→observe engine. Domain-agnostic. | `.intent/`, `spec/` (methodology) | Intent methodology |
| **3. Software Spec & Code** | Specs, contracts, and running code | `spec/` (generated), `src/` | The output |

**Six bidirectional data flows couple the layers:**
1. Knowledge → Notice: Lint surfaces signals (gaps, contradictions, staleness)
2. Notice → Spec (via knowledge): Spec authoring queries knowledge base for personas, journeys, DDRs
3. Spec → Execute: Trust-gated agents build against specs
4. Execute → Observe: Running code emits events
5. **Observe → Knowledge (double-loop):** Observations update domain models — questioning assumptions, not just optimizing
6. Observe → Spec corpus (single-loop): Spec drift detection, living doc sync

**Knowledge Engine schema:** `knowledge-engine/AGENTS.md`
**Knowledge Engine specs:** `knowledge-engine/spec/` (operations, federation, enrichment, redaction, boundary)
**Research archive:** `reference/karpathy-synthesis/`

**Owner:** Brien (theparlorhq@gmail.com) — solo practitioner, The Parlor
**Repo:** github.com/theparlor/intent (private)
**Site repo:** github.com/theparlor/intent-site → https://theparlor.github.io/intent-site/
**Status:** Methodology defined, CLI suite + MCP server operational, signal dashboard live, trust framework specced, signal management CLI operational (review/dismiss/cluster/promote). All 13 founding signals scored with trust levels.

## Core Concepts

### The Loop
```
NOTICE  →  SPEC  →  EXECUTE  →  OBSERVE  →  (back to NOTICE)
```
No sprint boundaries. No ceremony tax. A continuous loop where the team's energy follows the highest-leverage work.

### Four Products
Intent is four products, not one. Each phase of the loop is a product with its own maturity:
- **Notice** (Operational) — Signal capture from any surface. MCP server, CLI, GitHub Action built.
- **Spec** (Conceptual) — Shaping signals into agent-ready specs. Templates, CLI tools built.
- **Execute** (Defined) — Agent implementation against specs. Event schema defined, no integration yet.
- **Observe** (Schema-Ready) — Dashboard and learning layer. 15 event types defined, no visualization yet.

See `spec/product-roadmap.md` for the full four-product roadmap with investments.

### Work Ontology (7 levels)
Signal → Intent → Spec → Contract → Capability → Feature → Product

Each level has a clear owner, clear transitions, and clear events. This replaces stories, epics, and backlogs.

### Four Personas
- **△ Practitioner-Architect** (amber) — Senior ICs, system thinkers. Primary: Notice, Spec.
- **◇ Product-Minded Leader** (blue) — PMs, business context. Primary: Notice, Observe.
- **○ Design-Quality Advocate** (purple) — Designers/QA, contract quality. Primary: Spec, Observe.
- **◉ AI Agent** (green) — Claude Code, GitHub Actions. Primary: Execute, Observe.
  - **Authoring Provenance Sources:** Entire.io session traces, Granola transcripts, session-ledger md (feed Notice and Observe as event sources, not as agents).

### Event System
15 OTel-compatible events across 6 emission mechanisms. Events stored in `.intent/events/events.jsonl`. Schema: version, event, timestamp, trace_id (=Intent), span_id (=work unit), parent_id (=hierarchy), source, data.

### Three-Layer Repo Pattern (Extended)
- `raw/` — Immutable source material (research, analytics, competitors, support). LLM reads, never writes.
- `knowledge/` — LLM-compiled domain knowledge (personas, journeys, DDRs, themes, domain models, rationale). Agent writes, human reviews.
- `.intent/` — Work artifacts (signals, intents, specs, contracts, decisions, events, templates)
- `observations/` — Runtime feedback (metrics, incidents) that feeds back into knowledge base and specs
- `.claude/` — Agent reasoning (project context, session transcripts)
- `.entire/` — Authoring provenance (agent-session traces from Entire.io). One source feeding `.intent/events/events.jsonl`.

### Signal Capture System
A 5-tier adapter architecture for capturing signals from every surface where practitioners work:
1. **MCP Server** (Tier 1) — Claude Code, Cowork, Cursor. 7 tools: signal capture/list/get, intent propose, spec create, status.
2. **CLI** (Tier 2) — `bin/intent-signal`, `bin/intent-intent`, `bin/intent-spec`, `bin/intent-status`. Full suite.
3. **Slack** (Tier 3) — Reaction-based or slash command. Specced, not built.
4. **GitHub** (Tier 4) — Issue labels, PR comments. Specced, not built.
5. **AI Plugins** (Tier 5) — ChatGPT, Copilot, Codex. Specced, not built.

See `spec/signal-capture-system.md` for the full architecture.

### Signal Trust & Autonomous Execution

Signals are not just captured — they are enriched, scored, classified, and routed through an autonomous processing pipeline. The goal: work every signal as far along as it can go, with humans intervening only when something is unsafe or too ambiguous.

**Trust Model:** Every signal gets two scores:
- **Confidence** (0-1): How likely is this signal real and worth acting on?
- **Trust** (0-1): How confidently can an agent resolve this without human input?

Trust = clarity × 0.30 + (1/blast_radius) × 0.20 + reversibility × 0.20 + testability × 0.20 + precedent × 0.10

**Autonomy Levels:**
- L0 (trust < 0.2): Human drives — strategic, ambiguous
- L1 (0.2–0.4): Agent assists — enriches, human decides
- L2 (0.4–0.6): Agent decides, human approves — drafts intent+spec
- L3 (0.6–0.85): Agent executes, human monitors — full loop, observe after
- L4 (≥ 0.85): Full autonomy — circuit breakers only

**L0 Approval Gate (SPEC-APPROVAL-GATE):** External communication (Slack, email, PR, calendar) is governed by a typed approval protocol, not just prompt adherence. The gate intercepts L0 actions, constructs IntentApproval entities, and blocks until Brien decides. Configuration source of truth: `.intent/config/approval-rules.yml`. Methodology: `methodology/meta/approval-gate.md`. Gate skill: `platforms/claude-code/governance/intent-approval-gate/SKILL.md`.

**Three Human-Contact Patterns:**
- Phase gates (Notice→Spec): mandatory, prevents building the wrong thing
- Action gates (L0 approval): mandatory, prevents saying the wrong thing
- Strategic requests (`request_human_input`): voluntary, agent-initiated at any trust level

All three use the shared `execution.paused` / `execution.resumed` checkpoint protocol.

**Enrichment Pipeline:** Source Adapter → Dedup Agent → Context Agent → Trust Scorer → Classifier → Router

**Disambiguation Loop:** When an agent hits ambiguity, it generates a new signal asking a better question. The system never dead-ends.

See `spec/signal-trust-framework.md` for the full architecture.

### Deployment Topology

Intent supports a config-driven deployment model. The same tools work in two modes:

**Local mode:** `.intent/` in git is the source of truth. CLI tools read/write files. MCP server reads/writes files. Signal dashboard reads from git. Best for solo practitioners and teams that want full git control.

**Hosted mode (planned):** A service is the source of truth. CLI and MCP become API clients. Dashboard reads from the service. `.intent/` in git becomes an optional sync target. Required for always-on agent processing (Brien's laptop goes offline during travel).

Configuration lives in `.intent/config.yml` (schema in `spec/signal-trust-framework.md`). The same CLI commands, MCP tools, and dashboard work in both modes — only the backend changes.

The processing pipeline (enrichment agents, routing, execution) must run somewhere always-on. Options under evaluation: GitHub Actions (simplest), cloud service (most capable), dedicated machine (interim).

## Key Decisions (for context)

File placement within Workspaces governed by [/Workspaces/AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) — the authoritative placement resolver. Intent-specific knowledge artifacts follow the federation model in `knowledge-engine/spec/federation.md`.

> **Chainable atoms:** These 21 decisions are also represented as decision atoms in `.intent/decisions/DEC-INTENT-001.md` through `DEC-INTENT-021.md` for full chainability. The prose below is the human-readable summary; the atoms are the machine-traversable form. Both forms are authoritative — do not delete the prose.

1. **Named "Intent"** — not "Dev OS", Frame, Premise, or Lucid. The name IS the thing.
2. **Methodology first, tool second** — validate with practitioners before building software.
3. **Open development** — signals, decisions, architecture all public. Dogfood the observe layer.
4. **File-native, git-tracked, OTel-compatible** — no lock-in, no proprietary formats.
5. **Target practitioner-architects first** — senior ICs who feel the gap and have org influence.
6. **Specs as contracts, not stories** — agents need verifiable assertions, not prose.
7. **Staged GTM** — thought leadership → methodology product → tooling (conditional).
8. **Four-product framing** — Notice, Spec, Execute, Observe are distinct products with own roadmaps.
9. **Three-layer architecture** — Compiled knowledge base (Karpathy pattern) + Transformation OS (Intent loop) + Software Spec/Code. Independent layers, bidirectionally coupled. (2026-04-05)
10. **Compilation over retrieval** — The knowledge base compiles understanding once and keeps it current. Not RAG. Cross-references already there. Contradictions already flagged.
11. **Double-loop learning** — Observe updates Layer 1 (domain understanding), not just Layer 3 (execution). Without this, system can only optimize, never question. (Argyris)
12. **Origin tracking** — Every knowledge artifact carries `origin: human | agent | synthetic` for contamination mitigation. (Ango)
13. **Federated knowledge base architecture** — Core = universal substrate, engagements = bounded instances. Inherit down, promote up, never leak sideways. Mirrors Workspaces topology. (2026-04-05)
14. **Two products, not one** — Intent (methodology) and Knowledge Engine (product) are distinct. KE is separable — can be used without Intent. Brien's Knowledge Farm is an instance. The domain overlap is coincidental. (2026-04-06, DDR-005)
15. **Engagement rollout order** — Subaru → F&G → ASA → Cargill → Footlocker. Subaru first (most data, highest learning). (2026-04-06)
16. **Knowledge Engine as new MCP server** — `intent-knowledge` on port 8004 with CLI `intent-knowledge` (ingest/query/lint subcommands). Not bolted onto intent-notice. (2026-04-06)
17. **Retroactive enrichment = suggested** — Lint detects recompilation opportunities, surfaces as signals. On-demand execution. Not automatic cascades. (2026-04-06)
18. **Redaction at tool level** — MCP server applies confidentiality projection automatically based on engagement context. Not a flag Brien has to remember. (2026-04-06)
19. **Spec-shaping is self-prompting through personas** — Intents become specs through four-persona interrogation (△ Shape, ◇ Outcome, ○ Contract, ◉ Readiness). The system self-prompts with each persona querying the knowledge base. Brien reviews specs, not execution. See `spec/spec-shaping-protocol.md`. (2026-04-06)
20. **ULID-based ID generation** — All entity IDs (SIG, INT, SPEC, CON, DEC) are Crockford base32 ULIDs: `{PREFIX}-{26-char-ulid}`. Globally unique without coordination, timestamp-sortable, grep-friendly. Replaces the sequential counter that broke under concurrent writers and server restarts. Legacy `SIG-NNN` IDs remain valid via backward-compat regex. See `.intent/specs/SPEC-003-sig-022-ulid-migration.md` and `.intent/signals/2026-03-30-id-collision-distributed.md`. (2026-04-09)
21. **12-factor agent pattern integration** — Concept extraction from HumanLayer's 12-factor-agents manifesto. 5 gaps identified and resolved: pause/resume protocol (execution checkpoints), human-contact-as-capability (distinct from governance gates), LLM-as-judge (semantic evaluation in Observe), error-retry-escalate (platform-level standard), state philosophy (stateful system / stateless invocations). ## Agent Handoff Protocol

Intent is designed to be developed by AI agents (Claude Code) working from this file.

### Before Starting ANY Task

1. **Read these files first, IN THIS ORDER:**
   - `CLAUDE.md` (this file) — project context, architecture, tooling
   - `knowledge-engine/AGENTS.md` — compiled knowledge base schema, operations, cross-reference conventions
   - `tasks/ROADMAP.md` — **master execution plan with phase status, verification scripts, and contracts**
   - `TASKS.md` — living backlog partitioned by autonomy level
   - Any relevant spec in `spec/` or `knowledge-engine/spec/` for the domain you're working in

### Before Making ANY Decision

**Check existing decisions first.** Before choosing between alternatives on anything that outlasts today's task — a library, architecture pattern, API design, naming convention, or deciding NOT to do something:

1. Read `knowledge/decisions/` — scan DDR titles and frontmatter for prior choices on the same topic
2. Read Key Decisions in this file (§Key Decisions) — 18 numbered decisions with rationale
3. Read `knowledge-engine/spec/contracts.md` — 10 contracts that constrain implementation choices
4. **Follow existing decisions unless new information invalidates the reasoning.** If you need to override a prior decision, create a new DDR that explicitly supersedes the old one (`superseded_by: DDR-NNN`). Never silently contradict a recorded decision.

2. **Follow the ROADMAP.** It tells you which phase is current, what to execute next, and how to verify. Do NOT skip phases. Do NOT parallelize across phases (except Phase 4, which is explicitly parallelizable).

3. **Load context before acting.** Read all referenced specs upfront. Do not start modifying files until you understand the full picture.

### Execution Model

**Parallelize aggressively.** When a task involves multiple independent files or pages, use subagents to work on them concurrently. For example:
- Updating nav on 18 pages → spawn subagents per page or per pillar group
- Running contract checks → run all 10 contracts in parallel
- Building independent page sections → parallelize section creation

**Seek permissions and context upfront.** Don't discover mid-task that you need a file you haven't read. Front-load all reads, then execute.

**Verify before AND after.** Run relevant contracts from `site-contracts.md` before starting (to know the baseline state) and after finishing (to verify nothing broke). Diff the before/after contract results.

### Verification

Before committing, verify your changes don't break existing functionality:
- CLI tools: run `intent-status` to confirm the tool suite works
- Signal files: validate YAML frontmatter format
- Event log: check `events.jsonl` for valid JSON lines

**If something breaks:** Fix before committing. If fixing requires a design decision, generate a disambiguation signal.

### Signal Generation from Conversations
Brien may generate signals from Cowork sessions, Claude desktop app (iOS/web/desktop), or regular chat. These signals will be formatted as `.intent/signals/` files and committed to the repo. Claude Code agents should monitor for new signals and begin processing them through the enrichment pipeline.

### When Stuck
**Generate a disambiguation signal** — don't dead-end. Capture what's ambiguous as a new signal for Brien to review. Write it to `.intent/signals/` with `status: blocked` and `trust: 0.1`.

### Priority of Work
1. **Site roadmap** — read `../intent-site/tasks/ROADMAP.md` for the master execution plan. It has phased work with verification scripts. Execute the current phase before moving to product repo tasks.
2. Task specs in `docs/tasks/` — explicit handoffs from Cowork
3. Contract violations — fix any failing contracts
4. Signals with trust ≥ 0.6 that can be auto-executed (L3/L4)
5. Signals that need enrichment (add context, compute trust)
6. Specs that are approved and ready for execution
7. Infrastructure work (tooling, pipeline, config)

Never use em-dashes, en-dashes, or arrow glyphs (the long dash, the mid dash, the right-arrow, the ellipsis character) in ANY material Brien may share or that reaches peers/clients: Slack, email, Jira comments, Confluence, drafted notes, deliverable docs, suggested language. Use periods, commas, colons, parentheses, or the words "to" / "vs" / a plain hyphen instead.

Their presence undermines his confidence in sharing Claude-produced material, which is the whole point of producing it. This recurred 5+ times in a single session (2026-06-19, Subaru TechShare QA thread) despite the preference being obvious. It is a generation habit, not a one-off, so it needs a mechanism, not just a note.

**How to apply:** Self-check every drafted message, comment, and doc before presenting it. Consciously suppress the em-dash reflex when composing client-facing text. If stripping glyphs from an existing file, run the mechanical replace AND then fix the resulting comma-splices by hand (periods/colons/parentheses), because a blind swap leaves splices that read just as unpolished as the dashes did. Apply to the whole deliverable, not only the quoted blocks, since any part can be lifted and shared. Related: [[feedback_deliver_markdown_inline_paste]], [[feedback_subaru_esl_plain_voice]].

gh pr create --title "governance: bullet-glyph carve-out for markdown-stripping platforms (WS-DDR-121)" --body "Brien challenged the no-glyph rule as over-broad for LinkedIn bullets, and the measurement backed him up.

## The measured split

On LINKEDIN_EXPERIENCE_REWRITE.md: **59 arrows, 52 of them line-initial list markers**, against **69 em-dashes and 13 en-dashes sitting mid-sentence inside prose**.

The dash-as-connector in flowing prose is the construction LLMs overproduce and the one a reader actually clocks. A line-initial arrow on LinkedIn is a platform workaround that predates LLMs by a decade, because LinkedIn strips markdown and has no list syntax. Banning it produced a worse artifact with no gain in the thing the rule protects.

There is also a reader-expectation asymmetry: email, Slack, and Jira are expected to be human-typed, so a machine tic stands out. A LinkedIn profile is known to be crafted, so a formatted bullet list is native there.

## Scope, deliberately tight

All three conditions must hold: arrow or bullet glyph (never a dash or ellipsis), line-initial, inside a fenced block. Only the leading marker drops from the scan, so an em-dash inside a bulleted line still blocks.

## Verified before landing

8-case table, both directions:

| Case | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fenced LinkedIn bullets | pass | pass |
| Em-dash in prose | block | block |
| Mid-sentence arrow in prose | block | block |
| Mid-sentence arrow inside fence | block | block |
| Em-dash inside fence | block | block |
| Unfenced line-initial arrow | block | block |
| Ellipsis anywhere | block | block |
| Clean prose | pass | pass |

Hook passes \`bash -n\` and runs clean on empty input.

|---|---|---|

| Mid-sentence arrow in prose | block | block |
| Mid-sentence arrow inside a fence | block | block |
| Em-dash inside a fence | block | block |
| Unfenced line-initial arrow | block | block |
| Ellipsis anywhere | block | block |
| Clean prose | pass | pass |

- [intent#11](https://github.com/theparlor/intent/pull/11) merged, the hook change

Both are catch-nets that fired on correct behavior, and the cost is identical: a check that cries wolf stops being read, and then it is not a check anymore.

**Your move:** the LinkedIn copy is clean and the rule is fixed. What is still open from the earlier work is whether you want the AI-forward rewrites (headline, About, Butterfly, Cogitate) pushed live, which is the substantive positioning decision rather than a formatting one.
